articles.title: "I'm just trying to do the best": Naomi Osaka reveals how daughter Shai helped her see life beyond tennis after mental health struggles
articles.summary: Naomi Osaka has found a new sense of balance in life, and tennis is no longer the only thing that defines her happiness.
articles.body: Naomi Osaka has found a new sense of balance in life, and tennis is no longer the only thing that defines her happiness. The four-time Grand Slam champion has spoken candidly about her mental health journey, revealing how becoming a mother has helped her see the sport differently. With her daughter, Shai, playing a central role in her life, Osaka is learning to value the moments she spends on the court without letting results dictate her happiness. Her latest admission offers a glimpse into the personal growth behind her return to competitive tennis.Naomi Osaka credits motherhood for changing her mindsetOsaka shared her thoughts after beginning her China Open campaign with a hard-fought victory over Maria Timofeeva. The 12th seed won 6-3, 3-6, 6-3 to reach the next round, but her comments about life beyond tennis drew attention.Asked whether she felt happier despite not adding another Grand Slam title to her record in recent years, Osaka pointed to a change in priorities. Her daughter, Shai, has helped her build an identity that extends beyond her achievements as a professional athlete."I mean, I think it's all about mindset. I feel like I'm definitely happier now. It's because, like, tennis isn't my entire life. I've managed to build a life outside of that. My daughter's a huge part of it. I feel like it's also a part of growing up. I think I was very sheltered as a kid. I literally ate, slept, and breathed for tennis. Now it's just like growing up being grateful to be able to play the sport, but understanding that nothing lasts forever. I'm just trying to do the best with the time that I have," said Naomi Osaka.The Japanese star's comments reflect a shift in how she measures success. Instead of allowing rankings and trophies to shape her entire outlook, she now places greater value on the life she has built away from competition.Her most recent Grand Slam triumph came at the 2021 Australian Open, where she defeated Jennifer Brady in the final. Since then, her journey has included challenges that extended far beyond tennis.Naomi Osaka's 2021 French Open withdrawal brought mental health into focusOsaka's decision to prioritise her wellbeing became a major talking point during the 2021 French Open. After skipping her first-round post-match press conference, she received a $15,000 fine and faced warnings about possible further penalties.On May 31, she withdrew from the tournament, explaining that she had experienced long periods of depression since her 2018 US Open victory. She also described the anxiety she felt before speaking publicly."This isn't a situation I ever imagined or intended when I posted a few days ago. I think now the best thing for the tournament, the other players and my wellbeing is that I withdraw so that everyone can get back to focusing on the tennis going on in Paris."The truth is I have suffered long bouts of depression since the US Open in 2018 and I have had a really hard time coping with that. Though the tennis press has always been kind to me (and I want to apologise to all the cool journalists who I may have hurt), I am not a natural public speaker and get huge waves of anxiety before I speak to the world's media," wrote Naomi Osaka.She also explained why she had chosen to skip media appearances."I get really nervous and find it stressful to always try to engage and give you the best answers I can. So here in Paris I was already feeling vulnerable and anxious, so I thought it was better to exercise self-care and skip the press conferences. I announced it preemptively because I do feel like the rules are quite outdated in parts and I wanted to highlight that."Osaka later expressed her intention to work with the tour to improve the experience for players, journalists and fans.Her latest reflections show how her priorities have evolved since that difficult period. articles.title: Alexander Zverev crowned year-end world No. 1 after Carlos Alcaraz's shock Shanghai Masters defeat
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev has capped a breakthrough season by securing the year-end world No.
articles.body: Alexander Zverev has capped a breakthrough season by securing the year-end world No. 1 ranking for the first time in his career, becoming the oldest player to achieve the milestone for the first time. The German's historic achievement was confirmed on Monday after Carlos Alcaraz suffered a shock defeat to Belgium's Zizou Bergs at the Shanghai Masters, while Jannik Sinner's season-ending knee injury had already weakened his challenge for the year-end honours.The 29-year-old Zverev is currently ranked No. 2 in the ATP rankings but is assured of finishing the 2026 season at the top of the year-end standings. The milestone comes in a remarkable campaign in which he claimed his maiden Grand Slam titles at the French Open and US Open.“It's been a fantastic season for me winning in Paris and New York and knowing that I will finish the year on top of the rankings is just a dream come true,” Zverev said.“So much work and effort have been put into achieving this goal, especially after coming back from the ankle injury,” he added.Alcaraz's Shanghai defeat seals Zverev's historic achievementZverev's year-end No. 1 status was confirmed after Bergs defeated Alcaraz 7-5, 7-6(4) in the third round of the Shanghai Masters on Monday. The Belgian produced a composed performance to secure the biggest victory of his career and advance to the fourth round.The result ended Alcaraz's hopes of closing the gap in the year-end rankings and ensured that Zverev would finish the season at the summit. The German became the first player from his country to achieve the year-end No. 1 honour.Zverev's achievement is particularly significant given his previous near misses at the top of the game. He finished the 2024 season as world No. 2, but his success in 2026 has taken him to the pinnacle of men's tennis.Sinner's injury opens the door for ZverevJannik Sinner's absence has been a major factor in the year-end ranking battle. The Italian, who remains the current world No. 1, announced earlier this month that he would miss the remainder of the 2026 season because of persistent inflammation in his right knee.Sinner has not played since defeating Zverev in the Wimbledon final in July. His decision to prioritise recovery ruled him out of the remaining tournaments, allowing Zverev to strengthen his position in the race for the year-end top spot.The German's season, however, has been defined by his own achievements. After years of coming close to Grand Slam glory, he finally broke through at Roland Garros, defeating Flavio Cobolli in a five-set final to lift his first major trophy.He followed that triumph with a US Open title, defeating Ben Shelton in four sets to become a two-time Grand Slam champion in the same season.Zverev's remarkable comeback after ankle injuryZverev's rise to the top has also been a story of perseverance. At the 2022 French Open, he suffered a severe right ankle injury during his semifinal against Rafael Nadal and had to leave the court in a wheelchair. The injury disrupted his progress and raised questions about his return to the highest level. Four years later, Zverev has not only claimed two Grand Slam titles but also secured the most prestigious ranking milestone of his career.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India No. 1 Sumit Nagal apologises to local Portuguese crowd for post-match gesture: 'It wasn't right way to respond'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's No.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's No. 1 tennis player Sumit Nagal has apologised to the crowd in Maia, Portugal, and local player Henrique Rocha for making a “talking gesture” after his first-round victory at the Maia ATP Challenger, saying it was a heat-of-the-moment reaction.Nagal, who prevailed 6-3, 5-7, 7-6(5) in a gruelling two-hour-and-56-minute contest, addressed the incident in a post on Instagram. Rocha had served for the match twice before the Indian fought back to secure the win.“To the crowd in Maia, I want to apologise for the talking gesture I made after the match. It was a heat-of-the-moment reaction, and it wasn’t the right way to respond,” Nagal wrote.“I respect everyone who came out to watch, and I appreciate you being there. I’ve also spoken to Henrique and apologised to him personally.”The apology came after a fiercely contested encounter in which Rocha, who had won a title in Porto just eight days earlier, was looking to build on his recent form and collect valuable ranking points in his bid to break into the top 100.Nagal's response acknowledged the importance of respecting both the opponent and the home crowd, even in the emotional aftermath of a closely fought match.Disappointing Asian Games for IndiansThe incident comes amid a challenging period for Indian tennis. At the recently concluded Asian Games in Japan, Nagal was the country's last player in contention for a medal.India's campaign ended without a medal after he lost 4-6, 4-6 to China's Yibing Wu in the men's singles quarterfinals.The result marked India's first medal-less tennis campaign at the Asian Games since 1986, ending a run of podium finishes at every edition from 1990 onwards.India's doubles combinations had also fallen short, with the country's medal hopes disappearing after a series of quarterfinal exits.India had entered the continental competition targeting multiple medals, but the disappointing outcome raised questions about the depth of its current player pool and preparations for future international events.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Badosa: "Sé muy bien todo lo que doy por este deporte para que hagan comentarios en redes sin conocerme"
articles.standfirst: La tenista catalana, nueva embajadora de Laureus, cierra la temporada con tres torneos de la gira asiática y vive un interesante periodo de madurez personal y profesional
articles.summary: La tenista catalana, nueva embajadora de Laureus, cierra la temporada con tres torneos de la gira asiática y vive un interesante periodo de madurez personal y profesional
articles.body: Paula Badosa (Nueva York, 1997) es ahora otra Paula Badosa. O quizás sea la de siempre con la madurez que aportan los años. Atiende a MARCA desde Dubai, donde tiene fijada su residencia desde hace varios años. Y se la nota feliz y con las pilas cargadas, como si hubiera hecho las paces consigo misma tras los tropiezos del pasado. Sin duda, una gran noticia para el tenis femenino español. Pregunta. Antes que nada, felicidades por su nombramiento como nueva embajadora de Laureus. Respuesta. Era algo que llevaba mucho tiempo hablándolo porque es importante ser algo más que una jugadora de tenis. Todo el trabajo que hacen es increíble y quería formar parte ayudando a las nuevas generaciones. Ya empecé con esto hace un par de años en Nueva York y fue una experiencia muy bonita que me inspiró muchísimo. P. Qué importante es que los deportistas sirvan de reclamo en causas sociales, ¿no? R. Para mí es súper importante, más que nada porque pienso que a través del deporte puedes, digamos que entre comillas, sanar muchas cosas. En mi caso particular he hablado mucho de la salud mental y creo que el deporte en ese aspecto es un factor increíble, porque te aporta disciplina y resiliencia y te enseña a gestionar la frustración y las emociones en general. P. Centrándonos ya en el aspecto deportivo, vuelve la próxima semana en Osaka, ¿verdad? R. Eso es, para los tres torneos que restan de la gira asiática. La verdad es que estoy ilusionada. Quiero terminar el año lo mejor posible y mirando ya el 2027 con muchas ganas. P. Normalmente suele llegar a esta parte de la temporada con problemas físicos. De hecho, el año pasado cerró el curso en Pekín a finales de septiembre. ¿Cómo está? R. El cuerpo obviamente tiene sus cosas y yo vengo arrastrando muchas lesiones en mi carrera, pero esta temporada, dentro de todo, he tenido un buen año en ese aspecto y ahora me siento muy bien físicamente. Espero además seguir en esa línea para el año que viene escalar en el ranking hasta donde estaba antes y donde creo que debo estar. P. ¿Su objetivo hasta final de curso es acercarse a los puestos que le permitirían estar entre las 32 favoritas para el Open de Australia? R. ¿Por qué no? Obviamente siempre va a ser un objetivo estar mejor en el ranking y voy a preferir estar la 30 que la 50, y la 5 que la 10. Por otro lado, tampoco me preocupa mucho porque en los Grand Slam pasan muchas cosas y cualquiera puede ganar a cualquiera y si yo estoy bien, considero que puedo hacer un buen papel estando o no de cabeza de serie. P. ¿Le molesta estar la 58 del mundo cuando su tenis, en plenitud, es de 'top10’? R. Sí, obviamente me frustra, pero también entiendo y acepto por qué estoy en este ranking. Es evidente que me ha faltado regularidad en los últimos tiempos y que tengo que mejorar paso a paso siguiendo mi camino, pero también sé que al final las cosas caen por su propio peso. P. Siempre ha dicho que su objetivo es ganar un Grand Slam. El mes que viene cumplirá 29 años. ¿Lo ve todavía posible? R. Sí, siempre será así hasta el día que me retire, me lo pregunten con 20, 29 ó 35 años. Hasta el último día que juegue un partido va a ser mi objetivo, más que nada porque soy una persona ambiciosa que necesita objetivos grandes. P. España acaba de jugar la fase final de la Billie Jean King Cup llegando a semifinales. ¿Es una competición que le hace ilusión ganar o prefiere un oro olímpico? R. Representar a mi país siempre me hace muchísima ilusión, de una manera u otra, pero creo que al final tener un oro olímpico es algo que cualquier deportista sueña, ¿no? P. ¿Piensa a veces hasta dónde hubiera llegado Paula Badosa si le hubieran respetado más las lesiones? R. Puedo pensarlo alguna vez, está claro, pero luego también pienso lo que he conseguido con todo eso, teniendo lesiones y estando meses sin jugar, para volver a estar arriba. Entonces también estoy orgullosa de todo el camino. El ser humano siempre piensa "y si no hubiese tenido esto", pero soy positiva y sé que me quedan muchas cosas por vivir en el tenis. Me gusta más pensar de esa manera. P. En el tenis masculino, tras el 'Big Three' llegaron de inmediato Sinner y Alcaraz pero da la sensación que Serena Williams no ha tenido aún una heredera... R. Para mí sí que hubo un momento en el que Iga Swiatek estuvo ganando muchos torneos y marcando diferencias y ha habido después otro momento en el que Aryna Sabalenka también ha marcado diferencias, pero la realidad ahora es que el tenis femenino se ha igualado por arriba con 20 ó 30 jugadores de un nivel altísimo, cosa que no veo que pase en el masculino, porque hay menos regularidad en ese 'top 20'. Eso no pasaba en los años del 'Big Three'. P. Ha mencionado a Sabalenka, que ahora está atravesando un pequeño bache. ¿Le ha dado algún consejo como ella suele hacer con usted? R. Obviamente cada uno está su propia piel, pero he estado hablando mucho con ella y sabe que siempre va a tener mi apoyo, como yo lo tengo de ella. Tenemos una relación bonita y sana, que es algo difícil de encontrar en rivales de un mismo deporte. P. Usted es una persona muy emocional pero da la sensación de que ahora está gestionando mucho mejor sus sentimientos en la pista. R. Me gusta este análisis y estoy bastante de acuerdo contigo. Siempre voy a ser una jugadora muy pasional y emocional, eso no va a cambiar, pero he trabajado mucho la gestión de las emociones y la edad también te aporta experiencia. Me hago mayor, ¿sabes? [ríe] He sido una jugadora que todos los partidos que perdía lo magnificaba y dramatizaba mucho y siempre lloraba y quizá ahora me ves perder y puedo analizarlo sin hablar desde la emoción. Entonces creo que en eso he dado un cambio, un paso hacia adelante. P. Mucha gente en España la admira y respeta pero también hay gente que parece que está esperando cualquier derrota para arremeter contra usted en las redes sociales. ¿Ha aprendido a gestionar eso? R. Sí, no tiene nada que ver la manera en que lo gestiono ahora porque cuando he perdido ya sé lo que me espera en ese aspecto. Como jugadora emocional, me han afectado mucho los comentarios porque me los llevaba todo a lo personal pero ahora me intento quedar con lo que mi equipo me dice. Con el tiempo he entendido que es parte de a lo que me dedico y que hay gente que desafortunadamente vuelca su frustración en las redes sociales. Cosa que no deberían hacer porque al final no dejan de hablar o juzgar a una persona que es muy joven también y que está intentando dar su cien por cien. Yo sé muy bien las horas que pongo o todo lo que doy por este deporte como para que alguien me venga a decir un comentario sin conocerme o porque suba una foto en mi cuenta y me diga que dejo de ser profesional ¿no? Entonces, en ese aspecto he aprendido mucho a coger distancia.

articles.title: Jódar y el registro que le iguala a Djokovic en los Masters 1000
articles.standfirst: Es el tenista más joven, desde el serbio en 2007, que se mete en octavos de final en cinco torneos consecutivos de esta categoría y puede ser el más precoz de siempre si lo logra en París
articles.summary: Es el tenista más joven, desde el serbio en 2007, que se mete en octavos de final en cinco torneos consecutivos de esta categoría y puede ser el más precoz de siempre si lo logra en París
articles.body: Rafa Jódar acumula hito tras hito en su primer año en el circuito profesional. Cuando estrenó su casillero de torneos ATP, con su triunfo en el Open 250 de Marrakech, se convirtió en el ganador más precoz en la historia de este torneo. Cuando llegó a los 50 partidos en el circuito, presentó el mejor balance de la Era Open con 36 victorias y 14 derrotas. Su devenir en el Masters 1000 de Shanghái ha permitido presenciar un registro que no se veía en el circuito desde 2007 con Novak Djokovic. Jódar es el segundo jugador más joven en alcanzar los octavos de final en cinco torneos ATP Masters 1000 consecutivos. Novak pisó como mínimo esa ronda en Indian Wells, Miami, Montecarlo, Roma, y Hamburgo (en mayo, cinco días antes de cumplir los 20 años, jugó y ganó los octavos ante Nieminen y luego perdió en cuartos ante Moyá). Añadiría una presencia consecutiva más en Canadá casi dos meses después. Jódar ha logrado esas cinco clasificaciones para octavos con 20 años y 25 días. Si tomamos como medida cuando juegue esta ronda en Shanghái (este miércoles a las 6:00 horas peninsulares) lo hará con 20 años y 27 días. Tiene en su mano, si logra también pisar esta ronda en el Masters 1000 París, ser el más joven en llegar a seis octavos seguidos ya que lo haría con 20 años pero unos cuantos días que cuando Djokovic jugó con Nabaldian en Montreal en agosto de 2007 (20 años, 2 meses y 18 días). Tras su remontada ante Jiri Lehecka, Jódar se medirá a Botic van de Zandschulp. El tenista madrileño va en camino de conseguir otro hito: jugar las ATP Finals en su primer año como profesional. Ni Nadal ni Djokovic (tardaron tres años) ni Federer (cuatro años) ni Alcaraz ni Sinner (dos años) lo lograron en su debut en el circuito ATP.

articles.title: Katie Boulter: British number one beaten by Diana Shnaider in Wuhan
articles.summary: British number one Katie Boulter loses to Diana Shnaider in the Wuhan Open first round.
articles.body:
British number one Katie Boulter is out of the Wuhan Open after a first-round defeat by Russian Diana Shnaider.

After a competitive first set, Boulter lost her serve four times in the second as world number 13 Shnaider convincingly won 6-3 6-1 in one hour and 30 minutes.

This has been a largely disappointing season for Boulter, who is ranked 54th in the world and has posted just two wins across the four Grand Slam tournaments.

Since suffering a first-round exit at Wimbledon in June, Boulter has won just three of the nine singles matches she has played on the WTA Tour.

This one came at a difficult time for Boulter, whose grandfather, Brian, died last week.

He was described by Boulter's brother James as "Katie's biggest supporter" and Boulter said in a social media tribute before competing in Wuhan that she had experienced "a tough week".

articles.title: Van de Zandschulp - Rafa Jódar: horario y dónde ver el partido de octavos del Masters 1000 de Shanghái
articles.standfirst: El español busca los cuartos en el certamen asiático
articles.summary: El español busca los cuartos en el certamen asiático
articles.body: Rafa Jódar está recuperando las sensaciones ganadoras en Shanghái. Tras su desdichado debut en Tokio, acumula dos remontadas sobre las pistas de la ciudad china, ante el argentino Tirante (54 del mundo) y el checo Lehecka (16), en sus dos primeros duelos. En su primera temporada, el madrileño ha alcanzado la ronda de los 16 mejores en cinco torneos de Masters 1000 consecutivos. El más joven en hacerlo desde Novak Djokovic en 2007. En París (del 2 al 8 de noviembre) tiene la oportunidad de superar esta marca. Ante él tendrá a Botic Van de Zandschulp, actual número 41 del ranking ATP. No existe ningún precedente entre ambos. El holandés viene de derrotar a Dani Mérida (44) en su debut, a Alex Michelsen (35) y dar la sorpresa frente Arthur Fils (11). El partido entre Van de Zandschulp y Jódar está programado en el primer turno en pista central del Centro de Tenis de Qizhong, sobre las 6:00 horas en España. El duelo entre Van de Zandschulp y Jódar se podrá seguir por Movistar plus. Además de poder seguir toda la actualidad en MARCA.com y Radio MARCA.

articles.title: El futuro Nº1 quiere más en Shanghái
articles.standfirst: Zverev, tocado del tobillo, se lleva otro gran partido a tres sets ante Bublik y firma los cuartos en Shanghái
articles.summary: Zverev, tocado del tobillo, se lleva otro gran partido a tres sets ante Bublik y firma los cuartos en Shanghái
articles.body: Alexander Zverev volvió a ser protagonista en la noche de Shanghái. Sabedor de su futura condición como número 1 de fin de año, solo le queda seguir sumando victorias para serlo cuanto antes. Hoy, no ha sido menos. El alemán, tocado del tobillo derecho, ha derrotado al otro 'Sascha' del circuito, el kazajo Alexander Bublik, por 7-6 (6), 4-6 y 7-6 (1) para firmar los cuartos de un certamen por decimosegunda vez esta temporada. Una auténtica batalla de dos horas y 41 minutos de duración en el Centro de Tenis Qizhong. Los galones de Alexander Zverev se hacen notar en este tipo de encuentros. Aunque partía como favorito, el cara a cara, antes de la contienda, lo dominaba Bublik por 3-1. Y el kazajo siempre suele estar inspirado ante el teutón, pero hoy, esa barrera la ha roto el 'Sascha' número 1, que ya suma 40 cuartos de final en torneos de la serie masters, y 120 en su carrera. En el primer set tan solo se dieron dos oportunidades de rotura, una para cada uno. Debido al buen hacer al servicio de ambos, el tie-break era inevitable. Lo dominaba Bublik por 6-3, prácticamente acariciando el set. Pero para echar al doble campeón de Grand Slam, hace falta algo más que tres puntos de set. El de Hamburgo ganó los cinco siguientes y se hizo con la primera manga. Ya empezaban las quejas del kazajo hacia su palco. Aunque más tarde, aprovechó la primera opción que tuvo con 2-2 para romper el saque del germano e igualar el encuentro. Por un momento, Bublik le había dado la vuelta a la situación. Todo sumado a las continuas molestias que sentía Zverev en su tobillo derecho por tercer día consecutivo. El tercer set, tras dos 'breaks' en los dos primeros juegos, lo volvió a dictaminar el tie-break. En esta ocasión, Zverev fue simplemente mejor y le endosó un 7-1 a su rival para ser el tercer jugador en poner su nombre en los cuartos del TMS de Shanghái, junto a De Miñaur y Arthur Gea. Sascha habló del estado de su tobillo en la rueda de prensa tras el partido: "Empecé a sentir el tobillo en el último partido. En el calentamiento estaba bien. Al principio, en el primer set, también, me sentía bien. Pero cuanto más se alargaba el partido, a mitad del segundo set, empezó a ponerse peor", declaraba el alemán. Aunque confiesa que nunca piensa en la retirada: "Nunca me he retirado de un partido de tenis en mi vida, excepto en Roland Garros en 2022, cuando realmente no podía ni andar. Quería seguir, no me quiero retirar sin razones. Al final, luché y gané, y estoy contento". Esta es la tercera vez en la presente década que Zverev alcanza la ronda de los 8 mejores en cinco o más ocasiones en la misma temporada (2021, 2024 y 2026). Zverev tendrá en frente a Alex de Miñaur. El australiano viene de derrotar al ruso Karen Khachanov por 6-3 y 6-4.

articles.title: Nadal lanza el vino 'El Tenista' con la Familia Gil
articles.summary: Rafael Nadal, retirado del tenis hace dos años, aborda una actividad profesional novedosa para él: ha anunciado el lanzamiento del vino 'El Tenista', creado junto a la Familia Gil, de acreditada tradición viticultora y bodeguera.
articles.body: Rafael Nadal, retirado del tenis hace dos años, aborda una actividad profesional novedosa para él: ha anunciado el lanzamiento del vino 'El Tenista', creado junto a la Familia Gil, de acreditada tradición viticultora y bodeguera. "Hay proyectos que te hacen especial ilusión, y este es uno de ellos.. Desde hace un tiempo tengo la suerte de compartir con la Familia Gil una aventura muy especial: la creación de El Tenista, un vino que ha nacido de una ilusión compartida y de una manera muy parecida de entender las cosas. Me hace muy feliz poder formar parte de este proyecto, aprender de una familia con tanta experiencia y compartir con ellos este camino. ¡Espero que os guste tanto como a nosotros!", ha publicado el mito del tenis en sus redes sociales. Las bodegas Familia Gil, con base en Jumilla, tiene viñedos repartidos por casi todas las denominaciones de origen de España. Este vino 'El tenista' se distribuye en edición especial limitada.

articles.title: Shanghai Masters: Alexander Zverev celebrates becoming year-end No 1 with win over Alexander Bublik as Katie Boulter bows out of Wuhan Open
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev struggles with ankle issues but does enough to reach his 40th Masters 1000 quarter-final of his career in China; you can watch the WTA/ATP China Open and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Zverev, who won the French Open and US Open this year, never looked 100 per cent comfortable, and admitted his "ankle was acting up" following his win.

The top seed will take on ninth seed Alex de Minaur next after the Australian produced one of his best performances of the year to beat Karen Khachanov in straight sets 6-3 6-4 to advance.

Zverev said: "I'm starting to feel my body more and more, but happy to be through because it was a difficult match. He's been playing amazing tennis this week. I think the most important thing was that I won today."

With current world No 1 Jannik Sinner out for the rest of 2026 due to a knee injury and Carlos Alcaraz unable to overtake Zverev this year, the German was competing for the first time since he clinched the year-end No 1 honours for the first time on Monday.

"It is very, very special. To finish the world No 1 is a different kind of feeling," said Zverev. "It's a different kind of responsibility on your shoulders. I'm looking forward to that because I'm close to being 30 years old. It's a special feeling to achieve that."

Former British No 1 Tim Henman was full of praise for Zverev at the Laver Cup in London last month.

"You've got to earn the ranking points, and the way he's played this year has been absolutely phenomenal," he told the ATP Tour .

"He was a service game away from being in all four Slam finals. To have been working so hard and then not being able to win a Slam, and winning two this year and reaching the Wimbledon final, it's phenomenal.

"Twelve months ago, he had a tough time. He wasn't playing well, and he didn't play well in the Laver Cup. The transformation 12 months on is phenomenal."

Henman added: "When you see the way he's been stepping up in the big matches, he hasn't always played his best, but he's found a way to win. Then you give yourself a chance to play better. The way he's played in the Slams speaks for itself."

Katie Boulter was beaten by 11th seed Diana Shnaider in the first round of the Wuhan Open.

The British No 1 struggled to hold serve against Russian Shnaider, who reached the semi-finals of the French Open, and fell to a 6-3 6-1 loss.

Boulter, who has been mourning the death of her grandfather, began well and led by an early break but she was under constant pressure on serve and was unable to match the consistency of her opponent.

The 22-year-old left-hander, who beat Boulter in the 2024 Hong Kong final, is now 3-0 against the Brit and has 30 tour-level wins this season.

Swiatek aiming to end year on a positive note as WTA Finals spot hangs in balance

Iga Swiatek has played at every edition of the WTA Finals since ‌2021, but with the Pole running out of time to claim a place at this year's season-ending tournament ‌she knows the importance of going deep at her few remaining events.

The six-time major ​champion has won only one tournament this year at the Canadian Open in August and failed to advance beyond ​the quarter-final stage at all four Grand Slams.

The 25-year-old, ‌who won the WTA Finals in 2023, is 10th in the qualifying table for the November ​8-15 tournament at Indian Wells with only four of the eight spots still up for grabs.

"Obviously I'm aware of the situation and it would be great to get into the Finals, ‌for sure it's our goal," Swiatek said.

"It's the first time I've faced a situation like that, to ‌get into the finals.

"It's a challenge, but I feel like it's a positive one and I'm really motivated. There are still a few tournaments ahead."

articles.title: Davidovich demuestra su madurez en Shanghái
articles.standfirst: El español vuelve a ganar a Hurkacz dos semanas después y firma los cuartos del Masters 1000 asiático
articles.summary: El español vuelve a ganar a Hurkacz dos semanas después y firma los cuartos del Masters 1000 asiático
articles.body: El sueño de Alejandro Davidovich continúa vivo en Shanghái. El tenista español volvió a demostrar su madurez ante el polaco Hubert Hurkacz (1-6, 6-3 y 7-6 (6)), al que ya ganó hace dos semanas en la final de Chengdú, para ser el cuarto hombre en los cuartos de final del certamen asiático. Será la sexta vez de 'Foki' en unos cuartos de final de Master 1000, la primera desde Montecarlo 2025. Los dos jugadores llegaban enrachados a la pista central del Centro de Tenis Qizhong. Davidovich firmaba seis victorias consecutivas sobre tierras chinas, y Hurkacz, nueve en la ciudad china de Shanghái. Una de las dos estelas se iba a apagar. En esta ocasión, fue la del polaco. El malagueño tardó 25 minutos en entrar al encuentro, lo que duró la primera manga. Hurkacz aprovechó el sufrimiento inicial de su rival, que tan solo pudo sumar 11 puntos al servicio. El polaco, sin embargo, se mostró impecable con este y lo aprovechó para firmar un abultado 6-1. En el segundo set cambiaron las cosas. La derecha de 'Foki' aterrizó en el partido y con ella, la confianza. A pesar del alto porcentaje de primeros de Hurkacz (82%), Davidovich quebró hasta en dos ocasiones su saque. La segunda fue crucial para firmar el set (6-3). Por decimosegunda vez en la semana, los aficionados asiáticos verían la manga definitiva en la pista central del complejo tenístico. El tercer set fue el más igualado de todos. Hurkacz, seguro en sus turnos al servicio, y Davidovich elevando el número de golpes ganadores a 34. Un revés paralelo ganador en el tie-break decidió que el español volviese a derrotar al polaco en una ciudad china. La próxima cita del español será en los cuartos de final ante el sorpresivo Arthur Gea, situado en el puesto 44 del ranking. Tras derrotar a Jakub Mensik por 7-6 (4) y 6-4, es la primera vez que el francés se mete entre las 50 primeras raquetas.

articles.title: Andy Roddick identifies issue Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz are having as they chase multiple Grand Slams
articles.summary: Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz won fewer Grand Slams in 2026 than they did in 2024 and 2025. The Italian won Wimbledon, and the Spaniard...
articles.body:
Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz won fewer Grand Slams in 2026 than they did in 2024 and 2025.

The Italian won Wimbledon, and the Spaniard won the Australian Open, but the other two Grand Slams went the way of Germany's Alexander Zverev , who ended his wait for a major title in style.

Former US Open champion Andy Roddick has now delivered his verdict on Alcaraz and Sinner's 2026 Grand Slam campaigns, suggesting both players are encountering an issue that could stop them from breaking records set by the 'Big Three' before them.

Andy Roddick says Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner 'paid the bill' for years of success with injuries in 2026

"He has entered the conversation because of how brilliant he is on the court of how many majors is he going to win? Is it 12, is it 15, can one of these two [Sinner and Alcaraz] get to 20 like the icons and the Big Three?" he said during the latest episode of ' Served with Andy Roddick '.

"But also, [Jannik] Sinner's body went AWOL at the French Open for a different reason. He was able to win Wimbledon, so we know what his top level looks like. But in order to get to the pantheon of what he has deserved, the speculation for, your body has to hold up for a really long time."

Roddick then praised Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal, Novak Djokovic, and Serena Williams for their longevity, which guided them all to 20+ Grand Slam singles titles.

"The one thing that amazes me, on top of the level of the Big Three and Serena, is just how long they did it. How long their bodies held up. Just for a second, let's sidebar skill, mentality, the ability to play in pressure moments, but also just dragging your body across the finish line so many times," he said.

"We are seeing that it is not easy. I think Carlos and Jannik are showing that this year, on the back of three or four years of excellence and the best tennis in the world, there is always a bill to pay."

Alcaraz and Sinner shared the four Grand Slams in 2024 and 2025, but failed to repeat the feat in 2026, partly due to injury. Alcaraz missed the French Open and Wimbledon with a wrist injury, and Sinner skipped the US Open because of his knee problem.

Combined Grand Slams won by Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner

If Alcaraz and Sinner want to chase down the records set by the 'Big Three', they will need to remain fit, something they failed to do in 2026…

Andy Roddick has advice for Jannik Sinner as he ends season early

Alcaraz still has work to do in 2026, but Sinner is done for the year. Sinner ended his season early after withdrawing from the Shanghai Masters. The Italian hasn't played since Wimbledon and has struggled with a knee issue.

Roddick has now delivered his verdict on Sinner's decision, sharing what he believes Sinner and his team should work on over the coming weeks and months.

"If you are on the fence of saying I have got to world number one, won all these Slams, won Wimbledon, but my body was rough. If you have a knee injury and you are also trying to figure out all of your other bodily issues in the heat," he said.

"Well, let's say we take off until the end of the year with the knee injury and really invest the time in figuring out the other issue also. Can we kill two birds with one stone before we start in 2027? That would be a logical conversation if I'm in that camp. If you are not jumping out of your skin to get back on the court, let's figure out all of this in one sitting rather than rushing back.

"Without knowing anything, if I'm in that camp, I am looking at the macro view of all of the issues, rather than just this being a month-long knee injury and can I get back? I think that would be short-sighted."

Sinner struggled in the heat at the French Open this year, suffering a shock second-round defeat against Juan Manuel Cerundolo. Roddick believes he should address that issue, as well as his knee problem during the off-season.

articles.title: Badosa se queda sin entrenador: "Gracias, Paula, por darme esta oportunidad"
articles.standfirst: La relación entre ambos se alargaba desde abril de 2023 cuando empezaron juntos en Charleston
articles.summary: La relación entre ambos se alargaba casi cuatro años
articles.body: Paula Badosa, que se borró esta semana del WTA 1000 de Wuhan, volverá a la competición sin el entrenador que la ha acompañado los últimos cuatro años. Pol Toledo ha anunciado en sus redes sociales el fin de la relación entre ambos. La andadura entre ambos se inició en abril de 2023 en el torneo de Charleston. Toledo y Badosa se conocen desde niños. Marcelo Wieliwis, el primer entrenador de la tenista, le pidió a Pol que jugase contra ella y se hicieron amigos. Por eso sorprende aún más su separación. Juntos ganaron el título de Washington 2024, uno de los cuatro títulos que figuran en el palmarés de la jugadora de Begur. "Después de casi cuatro años juntos toca cerrar una etapa con Paula. Siempre valoraré todo lo que hemos vivido y aprendido juntos durante estos años. Gracias, Paula, por darme esta oportunidad", escribía el preparador catalán en sus redes sociales. La separación llega antes de final de temporada y Badosa no se ha pronunciado. Paula, que el próximo 15 de noviembre cumplirá 29 años, ocupa el puesto 58 del ranking y tiene previsto reaparecer en el WTA de Osaka (19 al 25 de octubre). Lo hará ya sin Toledo en su banquillo. Después participará en Guangzhou (26 de octubre al 1 de noviembre) y cerrará el curso en Hong Kong. Badosa, a pesar de sus muchos problemas físicos que ha arrastrado estas últimas temporadas, sigue con el sueño de ganar un título del Grand Slam. Así lo confesaba en su última entrevista en MARCA ya como embajadora de Laureus. Empieza la búsqueda de un nuevo técnico, con la particularidad que la española tiene fijada su residencia en Dubái. En la página oficial de la WTA figura su 'hitting partner', Carlos Silvestre como entrenador y Toledo ya es pasado.

articles.title: Indian teenager partners with Pakistan’s Muhammad Yahya to win tennis title, reviving Indo-Pak Express memories
articles.summary: Indian tennis player Amrit Vats and Pakistan’s Muhammad Yahya have teamed up to win the boys’ doubles title at the ITF World Tennis Tour Juniors J30
articles.body: Indian tennis player Amrit Vats and Pakistan’s Muhammad Yahya have teamed up to win the boys’ doubles title at the ITF World Tennis Tour Juniors J30 tournament in Djibouti.The pair defeated Thailand’s David Awayo and Saudi Arabia’s Ahmed Bahaa Srouji 6-2, 6-4 in straight sets.Their victory brings back memories of the famous Indian-Pakistani doubles partnership between Rohan Bopanna and Aisam-ul-Haq Qureshi, who earned the nickname “Indo-Pak Express” for their success on the international tennis circuit.A win that recalls the Indo-Pak ExpressBopanna and Qureshi became one of tennis’ most recognised doubles teams, reaching the 2010 US Open men’s doubles final before losing to the Bryan brothers.The pair won five ATP titles together, including the 2011 Paris Masters, along with tournaments in Dubai, Johannesburg, Halle and Stockholm. Both also reached the top 10 in the doubles rankings.Beyond tennis, they used their partnership to promote peace between India and Pakistan through their ‘Stop War, Start Tennis’ campaign. They wore specially designed T-shirts to spread their message and received the Arthur Ashe Humanitarian of the Year award in 2010 for their efforts.Amrit and Yahya’s latest achievement recalls that period when athletes from the two neighbouring countries could compete together despite political tensions.Can sport bridge the India-Pakistan divide?India and Pakistan have long shared a complicated relationship, but sports have often provided opportunities for people from both countries to come together.In recent years, however, political tensions have increasingly affected sporting ties.Following the Pahalgam attack, India adopted a tougher stance towards Pakistan, with even customary handshakes between players becoming a point of discussion in cricket.Pakistan, meanwhile, have also resisted playing matches in India across various sports.The doubles victory in Djibouti does not change the wider political situation, but it offers a reminder that sporting partnerships can still bring Indian and Pakistani athletes together.Whether more such partnerships emerge will depend not only on the players but also on how relations between the two countries develop in the future.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jódar pasa a cuartos de Shanghái con otra remontada y está a tres victorias del récord de Becker
articles.standfirst: El madrileño, verdugo de Van de Zandschulp, puede ser el tenista que da más rápido el salto del 'top100' al 'top10'
articles.summary: El madrileño, verdugo de Van de Zandschulp, puede ser el tenista que da más rápido el salto del 'top100' al 'top10'
articles.body: Rafa Jódar se ha clasificado este miércoles por cuarta vez para los cuartos de un Masters 1000 de los últimos cinco disputados. Su víctima ha sido Botic van de Zandschulp, por 6-7(4), 6-4 y 6-2, en 2 horas y 30 minutos. Esa regularidad le permite seguir aspirando a dos ilusionantes metas en el torneo de Shanghái: ser el tenista que más rápido pasa del 'top100' al 'top10' y situarse en las posiciones que dan acceso a las ATP Finals de Turin (15 al 22 de noviembre). Boris Becker necesitó 210 días en 1985 para situarse entre los 10 mejores, una vez se estrenó en la élite. Jódar tiene que ganar el título para superar la marca del alemán el próximo lunes 19 de octubre. Se cumplirán entonces 203 días desde que se metió entre los 100 primeros. La distancia con Arthur Fils, que cierra el 'top10', es de 541 puntos. El tenis masculino español es mayoría entre los ocho mejores de Shanghái. Y es que el joven Rafa se une a Alejandro Davidovich. Cabe recordar que el TMS chino es el único que se le resiste a la 'Armada'. La última vez que hubo dos raquetas nacionales en los cuartos fue en la edición de 2017, con Rafa Nadal y Albert Ramos. A Jódar, de 20 años, parecen no pesarle los 71 partidos a sus espaldas en su primera temporada como profesional. Ya son 54 triunfos en el curso, sólo superados por los 61 de Alexander Zverev, virtual número 1 mundial y que buscará un puesto en semifinales con Alex de Miñaur. De momento, el fenómeno de Leganés es el segundo más precoz en llegar tan lejos en el certamen, sólo superado por Jakub Mensik. El checo tenía 19 años y 1 mes cuando lo logró en 2024. Por tercer día consecutivo dio la vuelta a un marcador adverso. Van de Zandschulp se anotó el primer set para perder los dos siguientes. Eso ya le había pasado a Thiago Tirante y Jiri Lehecka. El neerlandés, que en 2024 fue capaz de derrotar a Carlos Alcaraz, en la segunda ronda del US Open y a Rafa Nadal, en su último partido oficial en los cuartos de la Copa Davis de Málaga, vio como su rival le rompía hasta cinco veces el servicio. El tenista del Club de Tenis Chamartín espera en la antepenúltima ronda del viernes a Casper Ruud (20). El noruego se benefició de la retirada de Felix Auger-Aliassime cuando el canadiense perdía por 5-2. A Jódar le quedan tres torneos para cerrar la campaña 2026, que podrían ser cuatro si está en la cita de maestros de Turín. Novak Djokovic, el tenista que le precede en la Race, está a sólo 131 puntos. Después de Shanghái está apuntado en Basilea y París y será el número dos español en la fase final de la Copa Davis de Bolonia.

articles.title: Wuhan Open: Sonay Kartal upsets Belinda Bencic to reach third round
articles.summary: Sonay Kartal upsets Swiss ninth seed Belinda Bencic to reach the Wuhan Open third round as she continues to build momentum.
articles.body:
Britain's Sonay Kartal upset ninth seed Belinda Bencic as she continued to build post-injury momentum at the Wuhan Open.

Kartal reached a career-high ranking of 44 last year but has slipped to 170th in the world after a six-month injury absence.

Having returned to action for Great Britain at last month's Billie Jean King Cup Finals, the 24-year-old reached the third round at the Beijing Open last week before beating Ukraine's Anhelina Kalinina in her opening match in Wuhan.

An impressive 6-0 7-5 victory over Swiss world number 12 Bencic sets up a match with Italian 15th seed Jasmine Paolini or 20-year-old Czech Nikola Bartunkova for a quarter-final place.

Former world number one Iga Swiatek also progressed, recording her 40th win of the season with a 6-2 6-1 victory over fellow Pole Magdalena Frech.

Kartal suffered a stress fracture in her back in March, which meant she missed three of this year's four Grand Slams - including Wimbledon.

The Briton, who reached the fourth round at her home Slam last year, was in good form before that enforced break.

That included victories over American top-20 seeds Emma Navarro and Madison Keys at Indian Wells, before she retired against Elena Rybakina in the third round with the back issue.

Kartal has made a positive return, beating Chinese 31st seed Wang Xinyu as she reached the third round in Beijing, and has now won four of her five matches on her return to the WTA Tour.

articles.title: Tennis fans cannot believe what they are hearing about Gael Monfils, ‘completely shocked’
articles.summary: Gael Monfils has shocked tennis fans after his name appeared on the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) Retired Players List. Monfils is playing his...
articles.body:
Gael Monfils has shocked tennis fans after his name appeared on the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) Retired Players List.

Monfils is playing his final season in professional tennis before retirement, which now looks to have come much sooner than expected. Many were expecting the ATP icon to take on the Paris Masters on home soil in early November, but that seemingly won't be the case.

As stated by the ITIA, those on the Retired Players List have "declared themselves retired from the sport and may not return to sanctioned events unless they have made themselves available for out-of-competition testing for at least six months prior to the event in question".

Tennis fans have now been reacting to the situation on social media, with the majority completely shocked by Monfils. His last professional match will, therefore, have been his defeat to Learner Tien in the second round of the US Open, where he received a wildcard.

Gael Monfils shocks tennis fans with apparent retirement

Reacting to his decision, one fan wrote on X: "Completely shocked. Sad that we didn't get to see him play one last time at home. What a career. Hope he is successful in whatever he decides to do next."

A second agreed, saying: "Seriously? I don't think anyone was expecting that. Didn't he want to say goodbye to the French crowd one more time?"

And a third commented: "How strange that he doesn't want to say goodbye to his audience and that they haven't prepared a little tribute for him in France."

Other shocked fans noted: "No! It can't be," "It must be a mistake, it's just not possible," and "Wow what a shame!"

And summarising the thoughts of many fans, another said: "Oh wow what a bummer! He will be missed. So fun to watch and a wonderful personality to go along with his amazing tennis!"

Rotterdam (Indoor/Hard) Montpellier (Indoor/Hard)

It is indeed a real shame that Monfils is apparently bowing out with very little fanfare, although perhaps it is what the legendary figure wants. He can hold his head very high after enjoying a glittering career on the court, having given fans so many unforgettable memories over the years.

The 40-year-old will leave the sport as a 13-time ATP champion with a career-high rank of sixth in the world. Turning professional back in 2004, Monfils boasts a 588-360 career win-loss record, with $25,254,080 in total prize money earned.

articles.summary: El juez de silla castigó al español con un 'warning'
articles.body: Rafa Jódar ha certificado su pase a los cuartos de final del Masters 1000 de Shanghái tras remontar el set inicial del holandés Van de Zandschulp. Un encuentro donde tuvo que tirar de épica por tercera vez consecutiva y la tensión afloró en la pista central del Centro de Tenis Qizhong. Jódar vivió su momento de mayor tensión en el inicio del segundo set. Tras ceder en el primero, y estar con 40-40 al resto, el español expresó hacia un recogepelotas: "Dame la puta toalla, coño". El juez de silla ecuatoriano, Jimmy Pinoargote, le cantó un 'warning' por conducta antideportiva. Tras esto, Jódar se dirigió al juez de silla: "Sabes toda la tensión que hay, no me hace caso, le estoy hablando y no le he dicho nada malo". A lo que Jimmy Pinoargote le respondió: "Entiendo la tensión pero así no. Pídemelo a mi, y yo se lo pido. No puedo repetirlo pero tú sabes lo que dijiste, así no hablamos con ellos", cerró el juez del encuentro.

articles.title: Wuhan Open: Britain's Sonay Kartal earns huge win over Belinda Bencic to set up meeting with Jasmine Paolini in China
articles.summary: Sonay Kartal beats world No 12 and former Olympic champion Belinda Bencic 6-0 7-5; Iga Swiatek also advances after defeating fellow Pole Magdalena Frech; watch WTA Wuhan Open and ATP Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports, with events running until Sunday
articles.body:
The 24-year-old made a flying start against world No 12 and former Olympic champion Belinda Bencic in the second round in China, going on to claim a 6-0 7-5 victory.

Kartal missed six months of the season with a stress fracture in her back, returning last month at the Billie Jean King Cup Finals in Shenzhen before reaching the third round in Beijing last week.

Bencic is the highest-ranked player she has beaten since then world No 5 Mirra Andreeva in the Chinese capital last year.

Kartal, who plays Jasmine Paolini next, told a press conference: "I trusted that I would be able to get my level back, I just didn't know how quickly. I did a lot of things right today but I still think there's a long way to go.

"I can produce the level, but can I sustain it? I think that's going to be the hardest challenge. I'm happy to be back, I'm feeling good."

'I think I saw snippets from my tennis six months ago'

Kartal swept through the opening set before Bencic, who was a Wimbledon semi-finalist last year, responded at the start of the second, taking a 3-1 lead.

Kartal battled back and secured the crucial break at 5-5.

"Super high level from me right from the start," added the British player. "A match like that it's always tough to keep the scoreboard pressure when you've come out firing.

"Very happy with how I played in that match, the composure. I think I saw snippets from my tennis six months ago."

Kartal is ranked down at 170 following her injury break but is already guaranteed to leap around 40 spots.

Seventh seed Iga Swiatek eased into the third round with a 6-2 6-1 victory over fellow Pole Magdalena Frech.

Swiatek dropped her serve in the opening game of the match but then reeled off 10 games in a row to take complete control.

Frech stopped the rot with a break of serve to get back to 1-4 before Swiatek completed the win moments later in an hour and 44 minutes.

Swiatek said: "I'm happy to get the first match on the centre court because I didn't get a chance to play there before.

"At the beginning of the match, it was point by point, but then I was happy that I started making less mistakes and I used my chances until the end of the match. For sure it was tougher than the score."

Elsewhere , Karolina Muchova came from 6-3 2-0 down to defeat qualifier Caty McNally 3-6 7-6 (7-1) 7-6 (7-4), while Jessica Pegula squandered three match points and lost to Jelena Ostapenko in three sets.

Latvian Ostapenko won 2-6 7-6 (9-7) 6-3 in an unlikely comeback against second seed Pegula, who had not played since losing in the US Open semi-finals.

American Pegula has done enough to qualify for the season-ending WTA Finals in Indian Wells.

In Shanghai, Daniil Medvedev defeated Stefanos Tsitsipas 6-4 7-5 to reach his third consecutive quarter-final at the event.

Medvedev became only the fourth player - after Roger Federer, Novak Djokovic and Andy Murray - to reach the last eight of the tournament in three straight years.

There have been verbal flare-ups in previous meetings between Medvedev and Tsitsipas down the years, including in the Australian Open semi-finals in 2022 - but there was no real drama this time.

articles.body: Se aprieta la lucha por una de las cinco plazas restantes para las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22 de noviembre). Daniil Medvedev ha dado este miércoles un paso de gigante para estar en la cita de los ocho mejores del curso. El ruso, verdugo de Stefanos Tsitsipas, por 6-4 y 7-5, se clasifica para los cuartos del Masters 1000 de Shanghái, el penúltimo TMS del calendario. Medvedev se mantiene octavo de la Race 2026, con 3.220 puntos, distancia un poco más a Alex de Miñaur, su más inmediato perseguidor, y echa el aliento a Arthur Fils. Cabe recordar que Daniil perdió la semana pasada los 200 puntos de las semifinales del Open 500 de Pekín tras ser descalificado en su partido con Novak Djokovic por dar un golpe fortuito a un aficionado presente en una de las primeras filas de la grada. El moscovita, el único campeón del certamen que resta en competición (se impuso en 2019), es el tenista con más partidos ganados en superficie dura esta campaña (33), uno más que Alexander Zverev, virtual número 1 del ranking. Sólo Djokovic (2012-16), Roger Federer (2017-19) y Andy Murray (2010-12) habían sido capaces de encadenar tres presencias en los cuartos de Shanghái. Medvedev, quinto cabeza de serie del cuadro, espera en la antepenúltima ronda del viernes al ganador del partido entre Zizou Bergs, verdugo de Carlos Alcaraz, y Tommy Paul.

articles.title: El Six Kings Slam cambia sus fechas por los últimos ataques en Riad
articles.standfirst: El torneo debía celebrarse del 21 al 24 de octubre en la capital saudí y pasa a finales de diciembre
articles.summary: El torneo debía celebrarse del 21 al 24 de octubre en la capital saudí y pasa a finales de diciembre
articles.body: Riyadh Season ha anunciado este miércoles el aplazamiento de la tercera edición del torneo internacional de tenis Six Kings Slam —inicialmente previsto para los días 21, 22 y 24 de octubre— a las fechas del 27 al 30 de diciembre de 2026. Esta decisión refleja el compromiso de Riyadh Season de ofrecer eventos deportivos que cumplan con los más altos estándares, tras evaluar los desafíos organizativos y logísticos que conlleva la celebración del torneo y su posible impacto en la calidad de la experiencia del público. Los últimos ataques sobre Riad, el último de ellos el sábado, que obligaron a cerrar el aeropuerto internacional, han sido clave en la decisión de posponer el evento que iba a contar con la participación de Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic, Taylor Fritz, Alex de Miñaur y Learner Tien, sustituto del lesionado Jannik Sinner. La pasada semana un ataque con misiles contra el aeropuerto Rey Khalid de Ryadh ya causó víctimas mortales y más de 300 personas resultaron heridas. La guerra que la monarquía más potente de la zona mantiene contra los rebeldes hutíes del Yemen, aliados de Irán, su tradicional rival, ha llegado de forma sangrienta a la capital del reino saudí. El aplazamiento a finales de diciembre abre la opción de que Sinner vuelta al cartel porque se espera que el campeón de cinco grandes esté recuperado de su dolencia en la rodilla. Cabe recordar que Jannik se proclamó campeón en las dos primeras ediciones y se marchó a casa con una raqueta de oro, con un valor estimado de 250.000 dólares, además de un talón de 12 millones de dólares. El aplazamiento del Six Kings Slam hará que Alcaraz tenga un parón de 21 días hasta su siguiente torneo, que será el Masters 1000 de París. Posteriormente, volará a Turín para las ATP Finals y después lo encadenará con la fase final de la Copa Davis. El objetivo es ganarlo todo.

articles.title: Six Kings Slam: Big-money tournament in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia postponed until December

articles.body:
The tournament, which is in its third edition and awards £1.2m per competing player and an extra £3.5m for the winner, was originally scheduled for October 21-24, but has now been moved to December 27-30.

The six players included for 2026 are Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Taylor Fritz, Alex de Minaur and Learner Tien.

The decision to postpone follows continued unrest in the Middle East and the recent bombing of the international airport in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh.

"The decision ⁠reflects Riyadh Season's commitment to ‌delivering sporting events to the highest ‌standards, following an assessment of the organisational and logistical challenges ⁠associated with hosting ​the tournament ​and their potential ​impact on the ⁠quality of the audience experience," ⁠organisers said in ​a statement.

Italy's Jannik Sinner, currently out injured due to a knee complaint, clinched victory at the Six Kings Slam in 2024 and 2025, beating Alcaraz in the final on both occasions.

Attacks have threatened to disrupt sport in Saudi Arabia, with golf's Asian Tour also saying it is monitoring the security situation ahead of the Saudi International in Riyadh next month.

Saudi Arabia ⁠is also set to stage the Asian Cup in ​soccer for the first time in 2027, a key ​test ahead of the kingdom's hosting of the 2034 World ​Cup.

It is also hosting the FIFAe World Cup, an esports tournament ⁠series held by world soccer's governing body FIFA, in Jeddah from October 16-25.

articles.title: Six Kings Slam featuring Carlos Alcaraz and Novak Djokovic postponed after deadly Saudi Arabia attacks
articles.summary: The Six Kings Slam exhibition event - featuring Carlos Alcaraz and Novak Djokovic - is postponed following a series of deadly attacks on Saudi Arabia.
articles.body:
The Six Kings Slam tennis exhibition event in Saudi Arabia - featuring Grand Slam champions Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic and Alexander Zverev - has been postponed following a series of deadly attacks on host city Riyadh.

Alcaraz, Djokovic and Zverev were set to travel to the Saudi capital for a three-day event starting on 21 October.

Australia's Alex de Minaur, along with American pair Taylor Fritz and Learner Tien, were also earmarked to play.

The event had been in serious doubt since Yemen's Houthi movement launched attacks on Saudi Arabia at the weekend, including a missile strike on Riyadh's airport on Saturday that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300.

Saudi Arabia's energy minister vowed a "serious" response after the kingdom's oil and gas facilities were also targeted by the Iran-backed Houthis.

Three Saudi Pro League fixtures - including one featuring Cristiano Ronaldo's Al-Nassr - were postponed on Tuesday.

Other future sporting events could be affected by the regional conflict, including Formula 1 races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

"The decision reflects Riyadh Season's commitment to delivering sporting events to the highest standards, following an assessment of the organizational and logistical challenges associated with hosting the tournament and their potential impact on the quality of the audience experience," Six Kings Slam organisers told BBC Sport.

Ronaldo scores after match delayed by missile alert

Saudi minister vows 'serious response' to Houthi attacks on airports

The ANB Arena which hosts the Six Kings Slam is also located in the north of Riyadh, about 31km away from the King Khalid International Airport.

The third edition of the lucrative exhibition, which was won by Italy's Jannik Sinner last year, has been postponed until 27-30 December.

The Saudi Pro League fixture between Al-Riyadh and Al-Hilal, along with Al-Ittihad against Al-Shabab in Jeddah, has also been pushed back until December.

Al-Nassr's trip to Al-Ahli, also based in Jeddah, has been moved to March.

The league cited "logistical considerations" for rescheduling the matches.

On Monday, former Manchester United star Ronaldo scored for Al-Nassr in an AFC Champions League match delayed by an hour because of a missile alert.

In golf, the Asian Tour said it is "closely monitoring the situation in Saudi Arabia" with its season-closing PIF Saudi International scheduled to take place at the Riyadh Golf Club from 18-21 November.

"We are discussing the developing situation with our partner Golf Saudi with respect to hosting the PIF Saudi International in Riyadh in November," the tour told Reuters.

articles.title: Six Kings Slam 2026 Rescheduled, New Dates Revealed for Tennis Event in Saudi Arabia
articles.summary: The Six Kings Slam exhibition in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, featuring Carlos Alcaraz and Novak Djokovic, among others, has been rescheduled from October to December 27-30.
articles.body:
The Six Kings Slam exhibition in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, featuring Carlos Alcaraz and Novak Djokovic, among others, has been rescheduled from October to December 27-30.

Turki Al-Sheikh, chairman of Saudi Arabia's General Entertainment Authority, announced on Wednesday that the tournament that was originally scheduled for Oct. 21, 22 and 24 was postponed for "logistical reasons," according to Amelie Claydon of The Athletic.

In addition to the headliners in Alcaraz and Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Taylor Fritz, Alex de Minaur and Learner Tien were scheduled to participate. However, Claydon noted it "remains unclear" if all six players will participate in the event following the rescheduling, as the late December days fall during tennis' offseason and shortly before January's Australian Open.

Jannik Sinner won the event and the $6 million that came with it last year but withdrew from this year's edition due to a knee injury. Sinner won the first two Six Kings Slams after it was launched in 2024.

Each player who participates in the exhibition that airs on Netflix receives $1.5 million with an additional $4.5 million going to the victor, per Claydon.

While Saudi Arabia ended its deal to host the WTA Tour Finals and Next Gen ATP Finals after doing so in the past, it is scheduled to host a new ATP Masters 1000 tournament. That could start as early as 2028, per Claydon.

If all six players do participate, this year's Six Kings Slam will feature the men's singles champion in three of the four majors in 2026. Sinner won Wimbledon, but Zverev took home the titles at the U.S. Open and the French Open.

Alcaraz's health was a major storyline this year, as he withdrew from the French Open and Wimbledon, among other tournaments, as he dealt with a wrist injury. He returned for the U.S. Open and played well, reaching the quarterfinals before losing to American Ben Shelton in a thrilling five-set match.

Shelton went on to reach the final before losing to Zverev.

articles.title: “Outrageous To Call Coco Gauff A Cheat” – Serena Williams’ Coach Condemns Racist Abuse Against American At China Open
articles.summary: Serena Williams’ coach, Rennae Stubbs, on Tuesday defended Coco Gauff after the American faced racist abuse online following a controversial point during the...
articles.body:
Serena Williams' coach, Rennae Stubbs, on Tuesday defended Coco Gauff after the American faced racist abuse online following a controversial point during the China Open.

Gauff defeated 16-year-old Sun Xinran in the third round of the tournament, but the match was overshadowed by a disputed hindrance call. Late in the first set, Gauff raised her hand and stopped playing during a rally, explaining that the electronic LED advertising boards around the court were flickering and distracting her.

Xinran appeared to hit a clean winner as Gauff stopped playing. However, after the chair umpire reviewed the incident and ordered the point to be replayed, Gauff won the replay and eventually secured the victory.

The decision sparked backlash on social media, with Gauff receiving racist messages and accusations of cheating. On "The Rennae Stubbs Podcast," Stubbs criticized the abuse and defended Gauff's decision to stop the rally.

"But if she lost the first set, would she have won the match? I don't know. But if there's a player that loses her first set and comes back and wins in three sets, I want to know more because Coco does it all the time. SHE also never complains. And I would argue that she might not have even lost that game if she lost that point. But the hate that she received on the internet was outrageous to call her a cheat," Stubbs said. (28:50 onwards)

She also added that Gauff was entitled to raise the issue with the umpire, although she questioned whether the American had noticed the flickering lights during earlier points.

"She had every right to be like, 'Hold on a second. I'm trying to reflex back this ball. The LED screens are flickering. This just can't keep going.' Whether I would like to know if she noticed it in the prior points, because if she had, she probably should have said something to the umpire. But she's well within her rights. Now, if she had lost that point, would she (HAVE) lost the first set? I don't know. Would she have won the first set? I don't know. We don't know." (28:17 onwards)

After the match, Coco Gauff addressed the controversy, rejecting accusations that she had cheated and expressing disappointment over the racist abuse she received online.

Coco Gauff received support from the UN Human Rights amid hate at the China Open

Coco Gauff received further support from the United Nations Human Rights Office after speaking out about the racist messages and hateful comments directed at her following the incident. In a post on X, the organization condemned the abuse and called on players, coaches, sports bodies and fans to stand against racism and sexism in sport:

"Racist messages such as those targeting #tennis player @CocoGauff online are appalling and illustrate that Black female athletes are specifically targeted for vitriol and racial abuse. There is no place in sport for racial or sexist slurs and abuse. Players, coaches, and sports bodies need to stand up for those facing such attacks, and fans need to push back against those who sully sport with racism and sexism."

Coco Gauff's China Open campaign ended on Oct. 7, when she lost to Elise Mertens. She is next scheduled to compete at the WTA Finals, which are set to run from Nov. 8 to 15.

articles.title: Roger Federer was vegetarian until 16; then what changed? When the tennis icon was told, 'You cannot just eat green stuff!'
articles.summary: Roger Federer became emotional as he celebrated one of the biggest honours of his illustrious tennis career last August, delivering a heartfelt speech at
articles.body: Roger Federer became emotional as he celebrated one of the biggest honours of his illustrious tennis career last August, delivering a heartfelt speech at the International Tennis Hall of Fame in Newport, Rhode Island.The Swiss legend, surrounded by his family, loved ones and fellow tennis greats, reflected on a career that brought him 20 Grand Slam singles titles, including a record eight Wimbledon crowns. Federer described his induction as one of the greatest honours of his life, adding that fame had never been his ultimate goal.“My goal was to spend my life doing something I love... with the people who love it as much as I do,” he said.Retired since September 2022, Federer was inducted in his first year of eligibility, capping a remarkable journey that saw him spend 310 weeks as world No. 1.Away from his achievements on the court, however, an interesting detail from the tennis icon’s younger days reveals that his eating habits once looked very different.Federer was a vegetarian until he was 16, before a meal with his Swiss Davis Cup teammates introduced him to meat.How Marc Rosset persuaded Federer to eat meatIn an interview with Coopzeitung back in 2017, Federer explained that he had avoided meat for years because the quality of food served at junior tournaments often left him unimpressed."At junior tournaments, you do not always have the best meat on the plate, so I gave up thanks until I was about 16," he said.That changed in 1998, when he joined the Swiss Davis Cup team for the first time. Switzerland were facing the Czech Republic, and Federer, then a young player in a supporting role, went to a steakhouse with his teammates.While everyone else tucked into their meals, Federer ordered rice and salad. His decision caught fellow Swiss player Marc Rosset by surprise.“Hey, Roger, this is a Steakhouse here, you can not just eat green stuff!”Rosset responded by ordering ten small pieces of different types of meat for the teenager to try. Federer discovered that he liked about half of them, and the experience brought his vegetarian phase to an end.How Federer developed a taste for fishMeat was not the only food Federer gradually learned to enjoy. He said fish initially failed to appeal to him because of its distinctive taste.His wife, Mirka, helped change that, with the sauces served alongside fish making it more enjoyable for him."Fish I learned more by Mirka (Roger's wife). The pure fish taste did not like me at first, but by the many great sauces this changed quickly," he adeed.Federer also admitted that cooking was not his strong suit, praising Mirka’s abilities in the kitchen."I'm really bad at cooking," he recalled. "Mirka is a fantastic cook. And back when I lived in a shared apartment with Yves Allegro, Sven Swinnen, and Michi Lammer, I was always the assistant."As he got older and his training routine changed, he said he had to pay more attention to his diet and maintaining his fitness.For Federer, then, a simple steakhouse meal became a turning point in his food preferences,, with Rosset playing an unexpected role in changing the future tennis great’s eating habits.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.standfirst: El francés, con molestias en el psoas, abandonó a los 19 minutos con 4-1 y dejó al malagueño en su cuarta semifinal de Masters 1000
articles.summary: El francés, con molestias en el psoas, abandonó a los 19 minutos con 4-1 y dejó al malagueño en su cuarta semifinal de Masters 1000
articles.body: Alejandro Davidovich ya está en las semifinales del Masters 1000 de Shanghái. El malagueño se clasificó este jueves después de que Arthur Gea tuviera que retirarse a los 19 minutos de partido. El francés apenas pudo aguantar sobre la pista y abandonó con 4-1 en el marcador después de haber recibido asistencia por una dolencia en el psoas. Davidovich, de 27 años, alcanza así por primera vez la penúltima ronda del torneo chino. Shanghái se convierte además en su cuarta semifinal en un Masters 1000, una ronda que ya había pisado en Montecarlo en dos ocasiones, en 2022 y 2025, y en Canadá en 2023. El español necesitó poco más de un cuarto de hora para sellar un billete que le coloca entre los cuatro mejores del torneo. Gea intentó continuar después de ser atendido, aunque el físico terminó obligándole a detenerse con el partido claramente encaminado para Davidovich. El tenis español tendrá otra cita en Shanghái este viernes. Rafa Jódar buscará también un puesto en las semifinales frente al noruego Casper Ruud, en un encuentro cuyo horario todavía está por determinar. Davidovich sigue mandando señales al equipo español de Copa Davis después de su gran semana en Shanghái. El malagueño, que ha pasado en redes sociales del "Estoy eh" al "Esperando...", parece dejar clara su disponibilidad para recibir la llamada y viajar a Bolonia en noviembre. Su nombre no figura entre los cuatro primeros tenistas de la lista avanzada por MARCA, pero su rendimiento en el Masters 1.000 asiático podría hacer variar los planes de la selección.

articles.summary: El torneo en la capital austriaca se jugará del 26 de octubre al 1 de noviembre, previo al Masters 1000 de París
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ha decidido aceptar una 'wild card' para disputar el torneo de Viena, de categoría 500, que se jugará del 26 de octubre al 1 de noviembre, previo al Masters 1000 de París, ha anunciado la propia competición. El aplazamiento por la situación en Arabia Saudí del 'Six Kings Slam' junto a su precipitada eliminación del Masters 1000 de Shanghái han provocado que el ganador de siete títulos del Grand Slam aceptara la propuesta de disputar un evento que nunca ha ganado y que cuenta, en su cartel, con la presencia del número uno del mundo, el alemán Alexandr Zverev, el ruso Daniil Medvedev, el italiano Flavio Cobolli o el australiano Alex de Miñaur, entre otros. El italiano Jannik Sinner es el vigente campeón. El transalpino, además de vencer en la edición del 2025 conquistó la del 2023. Alcaraz entrará en acción el martes 27 octubre en la pista central de Stadhalle de Viena. El aplazamiento del 'Six Kings Slam', previsto para la próxima semana en Arabia Saudí y que se jugará a finales de diciembre, impulsó al director del torneo de Viena, Herwig Straka, a intentar reclutar al murciano para el evento y se puso en contacto con el entorno de Carlos Alcaraz. "Todo sucedió muy rápido, y Carlos aceptó jugar en Viena sin dudarlo. Me complace enormemente poder darle la bienvenida al Erste Bank Open este año. Es uno de los jugadores y personalidades más brillantes del circuito ATP y cautiva a una gran cantidad de seguidores en todo el mundo. Su compromiso es un gran honor para nuestro torneo", declaró Straka, encantado con este la incorporación. Alcaraz llegará a Viena el sábado 24 de octubre y comenzará allí su preparación. Su partido de primera ronda en la pista central del Wiener Stadthalle está programado para el martes 27 de octubre . La única aparición previa del español en el torneo de Viena fue hace cinco años. Ahora llega Alcaraz con 23 años y con 27 títulos ATP y siete Grand Slams en su historial. Esta temporada, ha ganado, entre otros, el Abierto de Australia en Melbourne, así como los torneos de Doha y Tokio. El torneo de Viena se disputará la semana previa al Masters 1000 de París, el último de la temporada de esta categoría.

articles.body: David Ferrer no seguirá como capitán del equipo español de la Copa Davis en 2027. Aunque su vinculación con la Federación Española de Tenis se extendía hasta final del próximo año, Ferrer ha anunciado en sus redes sociales que no seguirá en el cargo. "Los motivos de esta decisión son únicamente personales y responden al deseo de poder iniciar una nueva etapa", apunta Ferrer. "Quiero agradecer a la RFET la oportunidad que me dio de cumplir uno de mis sueños, como es poder ser capitán de Copa Davis de mi país. También quiero dar las gracias a todos los jugadores y a todas las personas que me han acompañado durante esta aventura. Ha sido un privilegio compartir este camino con todos ellos", comenta Ferrer. David Ferrer cerrará su etapa al frente del equipo de la Davis en la Final a 8 que se celebrará en Bolonia (Italia) del 24 al 29 de noviembre. "A partir de ahora, estoy únicamente motivado e ilusionado por poder guiar al equipo español a por otra Ensaladera. Tenemos por delante un reto muy bonito en Bolonia, donde, como siempre, solo ellos, los jugadores, volverán a ser los verdaderos protagonistas", escribe Ferrer en su comunicado. Una de sus últimas decisiones será la composición del equipo para esta cita. Aunque la convocatoria oficial será el 26 de octubre, tal y como adelantó MARCA, Carlos Alcaraz y Rafa Jódar estarán para los individuales, y Marcel Granollers junto a Pedro Martínez para el dobles. Queda una plaza, a la que optan Jaume Munar, Alejandro Davidovich y Dani Mérida, y que decidirá tras el Masters 1000 de París. David Ferrer llegó al cargo de capitán del equipo española de la Copa Davis en 2023 cuando tomó el testigo de Sergi Bruguera. En mayo de 2025 había renovado por dos años su contrato que finalizaba en diciembre. En su primera Copa Davis, España cayó en la Fase de Grupos disputada en Málaga. Al año siguiente, se metió en la Final a 8 en la que fue la despedida de Nadal del tenis. España cayó en cuartos de final ante Países Bajos. En 2025 se metió en la final que se llevó Italia. "Desde la RFET respetamos su decisión profesional y agradecemos mucho el esfuerzo y el talento que ha dedicado a nuestra selección. Como jugador ha sido una leyenda de nuestro tenis, y en estos años ha demostrado que desde el banquillo su aportación también ha sido extraordinaria. A él le ha tocado dar la alternativa a varios jóvenes jugadores que han debutado con el equipo español y que además lo han hecho con éxito. El tenis español ha estado siempre bien representado con su presencia y su profesionalidad”, comenta Miguel Díaz, presidente de la Federación Española de Tenis.
