articles.title: UN condemns racist abuse targeting Coco Gauff after China Open controversy
articles.summary: The United Nations has condemned racist online abuse targeting Coco Gauff after a disputed point during her China Open match against Sun Xinran. Gauff reject...
articles.body:
The United Nations' human rights office condemned racist online abuse targeting Coco Gauff on Oct. 10, calling for solidarity against racism and sexism in sports. The statement followed a controversial point during the American tennis star's China Open victory.

Gauff faced a wave of racist comments and direct messages after stopping play during a rally against Chinese teenager Sun Xinran on Oct. 5. The chair umpire reviewed the incident and ordered the point replayed.

The dispute quickly moved beyond the court. Gauff defended her actions and rejected accusations of cheating, while the United Nations and the Women's Tennis Association highlighted the abuse directed at her. The episode has renewed concerns about online harassment targeting athletes.

The United Nations responds to the abuse

The U.N. Human Rights Office issued its statement on Oct. 10 under High Commissioner Volker Türk. It described the messages targeting Gauff as appalling and highlighted the disproportionate abuse experienced by Black female athletes.

"There is no place in sport for racial or sexist slurs and abuse," the office said in its statement. It urged players, coaches and sports organizations to support those targeted and called on fans to challenge racism.

The response came days after Gauff publicly described the racist comments she had received. Rather than focusing solely on the disputed tennis point, the U.N. statement addressed the wider problem of racial and sexist harassment in sports.

The controversy began during Gauff's third-round match against Sun at the China Open in Beijing on Oct. 5. Gauff was serving late in the first set when electronic advertising boards around the court flickered.

Gauff raised her hand to stop play before Sun completed her shot. Sun appeared close to winning the point, making the interruption especially consequential. The chair umpire reviewed the incident and ruled that the distraction justified replaying the point.

Gauff won the replayed point and eventually defeated Sun 7-5, 6-1. The victory advanced her to the round of 16. However, the decision became a flashpoint online, where some fans criticized her response to the flickering displays.

The WTA's match report documented the match and the incident. It also noted Gauff's praise for Sun, whom she described as an impressive young player with a promising future.

After the match, Gauff addressed the online reaction on X. She wrote that people could disagree with her without resorting to racism, describing the volume of racist comments and direct messages as "insane."

"Lastly, I'm not a cheater or a thief," she added in her post. The statement directly answered accusations circulating online after the replayed point, while drawing a distinction between sporting criticism and racial abuse.

Gauff also explained her actions in a longer Instagram post. She said she noticed the advertising boards flicker and raised her hand when she was sure the distraction had occurred again. She maintained that the interruption was not an attempt to gain an unfair advantage.

Gauff showed respect for Sun after the match

Despite the controversy, Gauff spoke positively about Sun after their match. She praised the teenager's talent and said she had apologized for the awkward situation. According to Gauff, Sun understood the explanation.

Sun, 16, was making her WTA Tour debut at the Beijing tournament. She had earned attention after winning the U.S. Open junior title, and her performance against Gauff offered a chance to test herself against an established top player.

Gauff also expressed empathy for Sun's emotional response to the loss. She acknowledged how difficult such moments can be for young players and described sharing the court in front of Sun's home crowd as an honor. Her comments showed that the match's tension did not erase her respect for her opponent.

The WTA offers support and condemns racism

The Women's Tennis Association said it was appalled by the racist abuse directed at Gauff and was in contact with her to offer support. The organization's response reflected broader concern about online attacks that follow athletes beyond tournament grounds.

The WTA uses the Threat Matrix service to monitor public social media content. The system combines artificial intelligence, open-source data and human analysis to identify abusive posts, threats and potentially dangerous behavior.

The WTA and World Tennis reported in July 2026 that the service analyzed more than 1.2 million posts and comments during 2025. More than 12,000 were categorized as abusive, including 3,726 cases of serious abuse involving violent, sexual, racist or targeted threats.

The abuse affected Gauff during her next match

Gauff's China Open campaign ended on Oct. 7, when she lost 6-3, 6-3 to Belgium's Elise Mertens in the round of 16. Afterward, she said the online abuse had been emotionally draining, although she also acknowledged that her tennis had not been good enough.

Gauff recorded 8 double faults and 34 unforced errors in the match, according to reporting by The Guardian . She said she felt flat and lacked energy, but did not attribute every part of her performance to the online attacks.

The defeat came amid a demanding stretch of the season. Gauff had reached the U.S. Open semifinals before traveling to Beijing, and the China Open was another major event on the WTA calendar. The incident added a personal challenge to an already intense competitive schedule.

Online harassment remains a wider tennis problem

Gauff's experience is part of a documented pattern of abuse directed at professional tennis players. The WTA and International Tennis Federation have said that online harassment can include racist insults, threats, sexualized messages and attacks connected to betting losses.

The 2025 Threat Matrix report found that 35 accounts linked to 12 individuals were escalated to law enforcement. The service also reported that 66% of serious abusive posts were removed, showing that coordinated responses can lead to action even as the problem persists.

Sports organizations cannot address the issue alone. Social media platforms, law enforcement, tournament organizers and fans all influence how quickly abusive content is reported and handled. The U.N.'s statement called for collective action rather than leaving targeted athletes to manage the abuse themselves.

Gauff's career extends beyond the controversy

Gauff, 22, is one of the leading players in women's tennis. She won the 2023 U.S. Open singles title and the 2024 French Open doubles title, building a record that has made her a familiar figure at the sport's biggest tournaments.

She also won the China Open in 2024. Her success in Beijing has made the tournament a meaningful stop on her schedule, and her return in 2026 drew attention before the dispute involving Sun occurred.

The latest controversy should not overshadow the tennis itself. Gauff won the match in question under the chair umpire's ruling, then publicly condemned the racist response that followed. The U.N. statement broadened the discussion to athlete safety and the responsibility to reject abuse, regardless of disagreements over a sporting decision.

Fun fact: Gauff won the China Open singles title in 2024 , making her 2026 return to Beijing a return to a tournament where she had previously lifted the trophy.

The U.N. Human Rights Office condemned racist abuse targeting Coco Gauff on Oct. 10, 2026.

The backlash followed a replayed point during Gauff's 7-5, 6-1 China Open win over Sun Xinran.

Gauff rejected accusations of cheating and said criticism does not justify racism.

The WTA offered support and highlighted its efforts to identify and address online abuse.

Gauff's China Open run ended with a 6-3, 6-3 loss to Elise Mertens on Oct. 7.

articles.title: Wuhan Open: Sonay Kartal beats Jasmine Paolini to reach quarter-finals
articles.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal beats former Wimbledon finalist Jasmine Paolini in straight sets to reach the Wuhan Open quarter-finals.
articles.body:
Britain's Sonay Kartal continued her impressive comeback from long-term injury with a comfortable win over former Wimbledon finalist Jasmine Paolini to reach the Wuhan Open quarter-finals.

Kartal, 24, missed more than six months with a stress fracture in her back, but has won five of her seven matches since returning to action.

The former world number 44 ruthlessly brushed aside Italian 15th seed Paolini 6-2 6-0 with a performance that further validated Kartal's patient approach to recovering from the first serious injury of her career.

It was another statement performance from Karta following her straight-set win over ninth seed Belinda Bencic in the previous round.

"Against someone as good as Jasmine is, I knew I had to be solid from the start and not let up," Kartal said.

"From my side, it was a pretty flawless performance."

How patience has been a virtue for Kartal

Kartal was riding the crest of a wave in the early part of the season, having broken into the world's top 50, reached two WTA quarter-finals and recorded wins over top-class opponents.

Victories over 2025 Australian Open champion Madison Keys and former world number eight Emma Navarro in Indian Wells led to a meeting with now world number one Elena Rybakina in the fourth round.

However, Kartal was forced to retire with a back injury that proved more serious than first thought.

After initially hoping she would make a quick recovery, Kartal was left unable to brush her teeth without "being in agony", leading to some difficult decisions.

Missing Wimbledon was a particularly tough choice, especially given she reached the fourth round of her home Grand Slam in 2025, but resigning herself to not rushing a comeback has proved wise.

Her first match back a little over three weeks ago - representing Great Britain at the BJK Cup - ended in a narrow defeat, before she won two matches to reach the Beijing third round in her WTA Tour return.

"At the BJK Cup, the level I produced was much higher than I thought and I left super happy," Kartal said.

"Now I'm growing in confidence with every match I'm playing."

Using a protected injury ranking to play, Kartal carried that momentum into Wuhan.

She has not dropped a set in victories over Ukrainian world number 48 Anhelina Kalinina, 2020 Olympic champion Bencic and two-time major singles finalist Paolini.

Kartal maintained a high level from the baseline as Paolini unravelled with a series of unforced errors, securing a meeting with Ukraine's Elina Svitolina in the quarter-finals on Friday.

Meanwhile, Alexander Zverev continued to show why he is the best men's player in the world this season with a dominant 6-4 6-4 win over Australia's world number nine Alex de Minaur in the Shanghai Masters quarter-finals.

Zverev, now assured of finishing the season as the year-end ATP number one, will face Spain's Alejandro Davidovich Fokina in the semi-finals.

articles.title: La Rafa Nadal Academy abre un centro deportivo en Bahréin
articles.standfirst: Ubicado en Amwaj Islands, será el noveno de la institución en todo el mundo
articles.summary: Ubicado en Amwaj Islands, será el noveno de la institución en todo el mundo
articles.body: La Rafa Nadal Academy continúa ampliando su red de centros deportivos a nivel mundial con la próxima apertura del Rafa Nadal Tennis Center Bahréin. Ubicado en Amwaj Islands, el nuevo centro será el noveno de la institución en todo el mundo y se desarrollará en colaboración con HARVE, compañía impulsada por Infracorp y especializada en el desarrollo y gestión de proyectos de hostelería, ocio y lifestyle. Con esta apertura, prevista para el último trimestre de 2027, la Rafa Nadal Academy ampliará una red que ya incluye academias en Manacor y Kuwait, Rafa Nadal Tennis Centers en Costa Mujeres (México), Sani (Grecia), Hong Kong, Marbella y Punta Cana (República Dominicana), así como el Rafa Nadal Tennis Program en Egipto. A estos proyectos se sumarán las aperturas previstas en Brasil en 2027 y Lombok (Indonesia) en 2028. La colaboración con HARVE, que apuesta por introducir marcas y conceptos internacionales en el mercado bareiní, une su experiencia en la creación de proyectos de hotelería, turismo y ocio de primer nivel con el prestigio internacional, la trayectoria deportiva y la metodología de entrenamiento de la Rafa Nadal Academy. El proyecto se ubicará en Amwaj Islands, uno de los enclaves residenciales y turísticos más destacados de Bahréin, conocido por su entorno junto al mar y su oferta de restauración y ocio. En este escenario, el Rafa Nadal Tennis Center Bahréin aspira a convertirse en un nuevo punto de encuentro para los amantes del tenis, con una propuesta que integrará deporte, bienestar y servicios de calidad. El complejo contará con seis pistas de tenis indoor y outdoor, tres pistas de pádel, espacios de preparación física y recuperación, una tienda deportiva y una cafetería. El centro ofrecerá programas para jugadores de todas las edades y niveles, bajo la dirección de entrenadores de la Rafa Nadal Academy y siguiendo la metodología de entrenamiento desarrollada a partir de la experiencia de Rafa Nadal y su equipo técnico hace diez años. "Estamos muy satisfechos de ampliar la presencia de la Rafa Nadal Academy en la región con la apertura del Rafa Nadal Tennis Center Bahrain en Amwaj Islands. Baréin supone una incorporación importante a nuestra red internacional y estamos encantados de trabajar junto a HARVE para llevar al país nuestra metodología de entrenamiento, nuestra experiencia técnica y nuestra forma de entender el desarrollo de los jugadores. Esperamos contribuir al crecimiento del tenis en Bahréin, apoyar el desarrollo del talento local y ofrecer a los jugadores una experiencia que refleje los estándares y la filosofía de la Rafa Nadal Academy", afirma Joan Suasi, director general de Expansión Internacional de la Rafa Nadal Academy. "La apertura del Rafa Nadal Tennis Center Bahréin en Amwaj Islands supone un nuevo hito en nuestra visión de desarrollar destinos y experiencias excepcionales que combinen deporte y lifestyle. A través de este centro queremos ofrecer una experiencia de tenis de primer nivel, basada en una metodología de entrenamiento reconocida internacionalmente y respaldada por instalaciones avanzadas y entrenadores especializados", valora Abdulaziz Tawfeeqi, director de HARVE. Los Rafa Nadal Tennis Center constituyen una línea de crecimiento complementaria a las academias de Mallorca y Kuwait. Concebidos para integrarse en complejos turísticos, residenciales y deportivos de alta categoría, trasladan a nuevos mercados la identidad de la Rafa Nadal Academy a través de una oferta de entrenamiento que combina conocimiento técnico, atención especializada y los valores que han acompañado a Rafa Nadal a lo largo de su carrera. Su integración en este tipo de proyectos permite elevar la oferta deportiva y aportar un elemento de diferenciación respaldado por una marca de prestigio internacional. Este modelo, desarrollado junto a socios que comparten los estándares de calidad de la Academia, encuentra en la colaboración con HARVE una nueva oportunidad para acercar el tenis a un destino con una creciente proyección en la región.

articles.title: Wuhan Open: Sonay Kartal stuns Jasmine Paolini to set up quarter-final against Elina Svitolina while Alexander Zverev continues winning form
articles.summary: Sonay Kartal, in only her third tournament back from six months out with a back stress fracture upsets Jasmine Paolini in China; watch the WTA Wuhan Open and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Kartal has made a brilliant return from six months out with a back injury and dropped only two games in a 6-2 6-0 victory against 15th seed Paolini.

It was an error-strewn performance from former French Open and Wimbledon runner-up Paolini and Kartal took full advantage, winning the final 11 games.

The result equals the 24-year-old's best performance at a WTA 1000 tournament - the top level of the women's tour - with Kartal also having reached the last eight in Beijing last year.

"From my side it was a pretty flawless performance so I'm very happy with that one," said Kartal in her on-court interview.

Kartal's performances this week have put her on the verge of a swift return to the top 100 and she will next face fifth seed Elina Svitolina .

Svitolina broke Guo Hanyu's serve in the opening and final games of the match to beat the Chinese wild card 6-1 6-4.

Surprise French Open runner-up Maja Chwalinska is also through to the quarter-finals after a 6-4 6-1 win over American Iva Jovic.

"I think it was quite a solid match from my side," Chwalinska said in her post-match press conference. "Iva is an amazing player. I knew that I needed to play my best game to get a win today.

"I think we had many very challenging rallies and it was a very physical match, I think, even though the score maybe doesn't show it, but it was definitely a very hard match."

Diana Shnaider defeated sixth seed and Wimbledon finalist Karolina Muchova 7-5 6-3.

Iga Swiatek took advantage of the loss for Muchova as she kept up her push to qualify for the WTA Finals by grinding out a 6-1 6-4 win over American Ashlyn Krueger.

Winning the title would allow Swiatek to put pressure on Muchova in the race to the WTA Finals ahead of the season-ending event at Indian Wells next month.

Swiatek, who's reached the WTA Finals each year since 2021, is 10th in the race with the top eight qualifying.

Zverev reaches Shanghai Masters semi-finals

Top-ranked Alexander Zverev , who has been carrying an ankle injury, said he felt good on-court after beating Alex de Minaur 6-4 6-4 at the Shanghai Masters.

The German made 80 per cent of his first serves and saved all five of the break points he faced as he set up a semi-final meeting with Alejandro Davidovich Fokina .

"I felt both of us were playing really, really well. I was a lot of times outhitting Alex, which is difficult to do from the baseline because he is so fast and he loves this kind of court speed here," said Zverev, who secured the year-end No 1 ranking earlier this week.

"I felt good and I'm happy with the step up from the last couple of matches."

articles.title: Davidovich y su parón por la lesión de espalda: "Mentalmente fue muy duro estar en casa mirando"
articles.standfirst: El tenista malagueño desvela cómo afrontó el tiempo que debió de estar alejado de las pistas por los problemas físicos que arrancaron en Wimbledon
articles.summary: El tenista malagueño desvela cómo afrontó el tiempo que debió de estar alejado de las pistas por los problemas físicos que arrancaron en Wimbledon
articles.body: Alejandro Davidovich se convirtió en el segundo tenista español en activo con más presencias en una semifinal de Masters 1000. Su victoria ante el francés Arthur Gea, retirado por lesión cuando perdía 4-1, le mete entre los cuatro mejores de un torneo de este nivel por cuarta vez en su carrera, una más de las que suma Pablo Carreño. Por delante, está Alcaraz con 14 presencias. En la rueda de prensa posterior a su partido ante Gea y antes de saber que su próximo rival será Alexander Zverev, Davidovich recordó los dos meses que pasó alejado del circuito por una lesión en la espalda y cómo le afectó mentalmente este parón que le impidió jugar la gira americana. El dolor apareció en Wimbledon. "En el primer partido, tuve problemas en la espalda. Seguí jugando, pero no debería haberlo hecho. Estaba jugando muy bien, así que no podía retirarme. Después me hice una resonancia magnética y todas las pruebas, y tenía una protrusión, casi una hernia. Así que paré un poco. Después jugué en Umag y no le sentó bien a mi espalda. Tras eso decidimos parar para recuperar bien la espalda", explica Davidovich. "Pensé que jugaría Cincinnati y US Open, pero estuve tres semanas sin tenis, haciendo únicamente ejercicios de core y abdominales para la espalda. Cuando volví a jugar era muy difícil estar al 100%. No quería ir a Cincinnati al 50%. Quería volver con todo como hice en Chengdu", continuaba Davidovich. El tenista malagueño reconoció lo mal que lo pasó ese tiempo: "Fue muy duro porque quería jugar, pero mi espalda no estaba preparada cuando empezaba a jugar puntos. Y sí, mentalmente fue muy duro ver cómo los demás llegaban a las últimas rondas mientras tú estabas en casa mirando. Pero al final forma parte del proceso. A muchos jugadores les pasan cosas parecidas". Davidovich se sobrepuso y gestionó con calma este tiempo alejado de las pistas: "Al final, estar en casa con mi mujer tampoco estuvo tan mal, porque no pasamos mucho tiempo en casa. Pasar dos meses allí estuvo muy bien, con mi mujer, con el perro y con el equipo. Así que tampoco estuvo tan mal, aunque, por supuesto, yo quería jugar". Además de pasar tiempo con la familia, Davidovich también empleó ese tiempo para pensar en su tenis: "Estuve pensando en cómo mejorar dentro de la pista durante los partidos. Lo pensé mucho con mi mujer y con mi equipo. Si me quedan diez años más de carrera, pensé en qué quiero demostrarme a mí mismo y qué quiero mostrar a los demás. Así que sí, no fue una decisión fácil, pero ahora quiero expresarme, jugar de la manera que quiero y mostrarle al mundo quién soy". Davidovich jugará ante Zverev por una plaza en la final de Shanghái. Si gana se meterá por su segunda vez en su carrera en el partido por el título en un Masters 1000 tras el que perdió ante Tsitsipas en Montecarlo en 2022. En semifinales venció a Dimitrov. Sus otras presencias en el encuentro previo a la final de un torneo de este nivel se saldaron con derrota: en Canadá en 2023, ante De Miñaur, y de nuevo en Montecarlo en 2025, ante Alcaraz.

articles.title: ¡Suspenden 24 años a un tenista serbio por amañar partidos!
articles.standfirst: A Stefan Milicevic le han impuesto también una multa de 70.000 dólares
articles.summary: A Stefan Milicevic le han impuesto también una multa de 70.000 dólares
articles.body: La Agencia Internacional de integridad del Tenis (ITIA) ha suspendido al tenista serbio Stefan Milicevic durante 24 años y le ha impuesto una multa de 70.000 dólares, por infracciones graves de las normas anticorrupción del tenis, al reclutar jugadores para amañar partidos. La ITIA ha inhabilitado al balcánico, de 29 años, que creó una red de corrupción según una investigación que detectó la manipulación de seis partidos, cinco de ellos con él como jugador junto a otros tenistas. La sanción para este jugador balcánico, que alcanzó su mejor puesto en agosto del 2014, el 1.338 del mundo, entró en vigor el pasado 9 de octubre. Además de amañar seis partidos, intentó manipular otros tantos entre 2022 y 2024. Milicevic también fue acusado de reclutar o intentar reclutar a varios jugadores profesionales como parte de una red corrupta durante el mismo período, lo que resultó en que otros jugadores amañaran partidos. La sanción acabará el 8 de octubre del 2050. Aunque 24 años es una sanción durísima y casi sin precedentes, no es la más dura impuesta por la ITIA, que ha suspendido de por vida a varios jugadores, entre ellos el francés Alexis Musialek, la eslovena Nastja Kolar, la estadounidense Alexandra Riley y el búlgaro Karen Khachatryan.

articles.title: Serb tennis player Stefan Milicevic banned for 24 years for match-fixing
articles.summary: Stefan Milicevic is given a 24-year suspension from tennis - one of the most severe punishments outside of a lifetime ban - for match-fixing.
articles.body:
A player from Serbia has been given a 24-year suspension from tennis - one of the most severe punishments imposed by anti-corruption investigators outside of a lifetime ban - for match-fixing.

Stefan Milicevic, who reached a career-high world ranking of 1,338th in 2014, was charged with fixing six matches, including five in which he was competing.

The 29-year-old, who played on the lower rungs of the professional ladder, was also charged with attempting to fix a further six matches between 2022 and 2024.

Along with the match-fixing, the International Tennis Integrity Authority (ITIA) said Milicevic was also charged with recruiting or attempting to recruit multiple professional players "as part of a corrupt network".

Players who were recruited by Milicevic have also been accused by the ITIA of fixing matches.

The severity of Milicevic's sanction is partly down to a lack of co-operation in the investigation.

The ITIA said he "did not engage" in the process despite seven separate attempts from the independent organisation to contact him.

Milicevic, who also received a £53,000 fine, cannot take part in the sport until his ban ends in October 2050, by which time he will be 53 years old.

While suspended, he is not allowed to play in, coach at, or attend any events organised or sanctioned by World Tennis, WTA, ATP, the Grand Slams, or any national association.

In December, French player Quentin Folliot was banned for 20 years , external after the ITIA discovered he was a central figure in a network of players operating on behalf of a match-fixing syndicate.

Foillot, who reached a career-high of 488 in the rankings in 2022, denied charges relating to 11 matches which took place between 2022 and 2024, including eight which he played in.

However, at a hearing, some 27 of the 30 charges against him, relating to 10 of the 11 matches, were upheld.

articles.title: Serbian Tennis Player Stefan Milićević Gets 24-Year Ban for Match Fixing
articles.summary: Serbian tennis player Stefan Milićević has been given a 24-year ban for allegedly fixing multiple matches and recruiting other players into a "corrupt network," the International Tennis Integrity Agency said Thursday.
articles.body:
Serbian tennis player Stefan Milićević has been given a 24-year ban for allegedly fixing multiple matches and recruiting other players into a "corrupt network," the International Tennis Integrity Agency said Thursday.

The agency said the 29-year-old Milićević was charged with fixing six matches — including five of his own — and trying to fix six more between 2022 and 2024. He is banned from tennis until 2050.

Milićević never reached a singles ranking higher than 1,338 and only played in lower-tier events. But the ITIA also charged him with recruiting "multiple professional players as part of a corrupt network" that resulted in "a number of other players fixing matches" during those same years.

The agency did not give details about which matches were fixed, or name any of the other players involved.

It said Milićević did not cooperate into its investigation into the fixed matches and did not respond to its findings. It also fined Milićević $70,000.

articles.standfirst: Lideró a un equipo que jugó en Saigón tras la Ofensiva del Tet
articles.summary: Lideró a un equipo que jugó en Saigón tras la Ofensiva del Tet
articles.body: La Six King Slam está, de momento, aplazada. El pasado sábado un bombardeo causó víctimas mortales a pocos kilómetros del recinto que en dos semanas iba a acoger a las más grandes estrellas del tenis masculino. Recinto que, obviamente, está también en el radio de acción de los citados misiles, descubriendo así el tenis de golpe y porrazo, con perdón de la expresión, que ellos también pueden convertirse en víctimas de guerra porque las fronteras entre el frente y la retaguardia llevan mucho tiempo siendo difusas. Está por ver si en este año 2026 el tenis irá a la guerra. Pero hace casi 60 años hubo también quien temió que un misil pudiera impactar contra la pista en la que estaba jugando. Pero aun así saltó a ella. Corría enero de 1969 y los Estados Unidos estaban cada vez más empantanados en la Guerra del Vietnam, una guerra de la que teóricamente conocemos mucho gracias a la implicación estadounidense, que convierte todo en cinematográfico, pero que sigue teniendo todavía muchos episodios que merecen ser narrados más detalladamente. En ese enero de 1969 hacía un año que la Ofensiva del Tet había dejado sobre el campo 200.000 bajas. La gran mayoría fueron norvietnamitas, pero la acción había convencido a la sociedad estadounidense de que la guerra distaba de estar resuelta, como decían las comunicaciones oficiales: el enemigo seguía siendo numeroso, bien armado y entrenado y motivado. Pero aun así se seguía intentando 'vender' que la guerra era algo así como unas vacaciones aventureras. En la película Apocalypse Now se muestra una 'visita' de la estrellas del Playboy a las tropas, cerca del frente (un clásico de la guerra, en la de Ifni, en España, fue Carmen Sevilla)... La de enero de 1969 fue de otro corte. Las grandes estrellas del tenis estadounidense, encabezadas por un Arthur Ashe que entonces servía en el ejército y era en el primer negro estadounidense en ganar el US Open y formar parte del equipo nacional de Copa Davis, desembarcaban en Saigón para jugar exhibiciones ante las tropas de retaguardia, entre sí y con tenistas sudvietnamitas. Eran, desde luego, un equipo de primer nivel. Habían ganado la Copa Davis en 1968 -superando a España de camino- y repetirían en 1969, 1970, 1971 y 1972 con esa generación. Ashe era el líder del equipo. Ganaría también el Open de Australia en 1970 y Wimbledon en 1975. Y le acompañaban Stan Smith, Clark Graebner, Bob Lutz y Charlie Pasarell. Antes y después pasaron otros tenistas -entre ellos Gussie Moran, la primera tenista que vistió falda corta en Wimbledon, en los años 50, y que sufrió un accidente de helicóptero- pero la exhibición central y más promocionada -incluso se citó en MARCA- fue esa, a caballo de la 'militarización' de un Ashe que vestía uniforme fuera de las pistas. El evento se celebró en el Cercle Sportif, fundado durante la colonización francesa, y ya fuera por medidas de seguridad o porque no hubiera otras condiciones posibles, se jugó de noche y casi a oscuras. El árbitro tenía que pedir colaboración al público en las bolas dudosas. Saigón estaba lejos del teórico frente: la capital del Vietnam del Sur era una zona segura de retaguardia, pero en la citada Ofensiva del Tet las fuerzas del Vietcong se habían infiltrado en ella y nadie podía estar demasiado seguro que la victoria entonces obtenida fuera completa. Por tanto, la inquietud dominó durante el evento. "No me hubiera extrañado que nos hubieran disparado un cohete durante el partido”, dijo Ashe. Por fortuna, no hubo bajas, pero sí polémica. A Ashe se le criticó por su pertenencia al ejército o no hablar contra la guerra cuando Mohamed Alí estaba sancionado por negarse al reclutamiento. Se le calificó, desde los sectores más firmemente opositores de 'Tío Tom', como negro colaboracionista con un poder estadounidense que sólo a duras penas y en fecha muy reciente comenzaba a dejar atrás la segregación racial legal. Ese mismo año Arthur se pronunció firmemente contra el apartheid sudafricano y durante muchos años se implicó profundamente en causas sociales. Pasó por varias cirugías a corazón abierto por problemas cardiacos y durante una de ellas, en una transfusión, recibió sangre contaminada con el entonces casi desconocido SIDA. Falleció en 1993, a los 49 años. Hoy da nombre a la pista central del US Open. A Arthur, por cierto, le hubiera tocado ir a Vietnam como combatiente, pero le salvó de ello su hermano Johnnie, también militar. La ley estadounidense impide o desaconseja que varios hermanos estén simultáneamente en el frente –recuerden la película ‘Salvar al soldado Ryan’– y él, tras cumplir su turno en Vietnam, pidió un reenganche en zona de guerra para que Arthur, destinado en los Estados Unidos con el grado de teniente, no fuera a parar al frente. La guerra del Vietnam fue una guerra de infantería, de pobres como todas ("A la guerra me lleva mi necesidad", cantaba el personaje del Quijote y los Credence 400 años después) y con mucho aún por contar. La historia del Ejército de Idiotas de McNamara está por relatarse más allá de los libros de historia... Epílogo: El general William Westmoreland, mando supremo de las tropas estadounidenses en Vietnam, sufrió una herida durante la guerra: se lesionó en una muñeca jugando al tenis en el Cercle Sportif de Saigón.

articles.title: Stefan Milicevic given 24-year ban for match-fixing: Serbian player, 29, banned from tennis until 2050
articles.summary: According to the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA), Stefan Milicevic shown to have fixed six matches - five of which he played in - and attempted to with six more; Milicevic's suspension will come to an end on October 8, 2050, by which time he would be 53
articles.body:
Stefan Milicevic led a "corrupt network" of match-fixing between 2022 and 2024, according to the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA), with the 29-year-old shown to have fixed six matches - five of which he played in - and attempted to with six more.

Milicevic, whose highest ATP ranking was 1338, did not engage or co-operate with the investigation, according to the ITIA, and was also fined 70,000 US dollars (£52,800).

The ITIA's statement on Thursday said: "Milicevic was also charged with recruiting or attempting to recruit multiple professional players as part of a corrupt network during the same period, resulting in a number of other players fixing matches."

Milicevic's suspension will officially come to an end on October 8, 2050, by which time he would be 53 years old.

The ITIA added: "While suspended, Milicevic is not allowed to play in, coach at, or attend any events organised or sanctioned by World Tennis, WTA, ATP, the Grand Slams, or any national association."

articles.title: Mirra Andreeva takes playful swipe at Beijing crowd after heartbreaking China Open final
articles.summary: Mirra Andreeva joked about missing cheers after losing the China Open final to Zheng Qinwen in Beijing.
articles.body:
Some losses fade by the next morning. Others spark conversations that last for days. A single well-timed remark can travel farther than any scoreline, especially when it comes from a bright and rising star.

Fans love athletes who show personality. A match result tells us who won, but a quote tells us who they are. That is why small moments often matter most to the people watching at home.

During her runner-up speech, Andreeva thanked everyone who supported her all week. Then she said she thought she might hear one "let's go Mirra" during the final, but no. The line carried quiet humor.

Later reporters pointed out that many fans cheered for her. Andreeva agreed some people showed support. Still, she called it very hard to compare that backing with the loud roar for Zheng, especially that day.

The humor worked because it stayed gentle. Nobody could call it rude. A teenager had simply noticed a gap where cheers might have been, and she named it out loud with calm and plain honesty.

Zheng makes history in front of home fans

Zheng became the first Chinese woman to win the China Open title. She was the first wildcard champion since the event returned in 2004. The title was also her first at the WTA 1000 level.

The Olympic gold medalist had already reached a Grand Slam final. Yet a WTA 1000 title had slipped away until now. The Beijing home crowd finally had a champion of its very own to celebrate.

Last year Zheng retired from her third-round match at the same event. That setback made this return feel even bigger. Beijing fans had watched her struggle and now saw her lift the trophy high.

Andreeva started well and broke early to go up two games to love. Zheng soon leveled the score at two all. The crowd cheered each winning shot from Zheng while Andreeva earned only occasional applause.

Home crowds shape big matches. Every winner gets louder, and every miss feels heavier. Players on the other side must find calm inside a wall of sound, and that is very hard even for stars.

Andreeva knows that feeling. At the French Open final in June, she also had little crowd support, with one Russian shout of "Go Mirra" late in the match. She still won and lifted the trophy.

The numbers behind Zheng's winning serve

Zheng landed only 37.9% of her first serves yet won 72.7% of those points. She also took 63.9% of her second serve points. That left Andreeva little room to breathe when returning in the final.

Serving numbers tell only part of the story. Tennis also needs nerve and belief, and Zheng found both when the biggest points arrived. That calm helped her control moments in tight matches like this one.

Andreeva still has plenty of time to fix these details. Young players often grow fastest after painful finals like this. One tough Sunday in Beijing will not erase the talent that fans can clearly see.

After her win, Zheng sang a little karaoke in front of thousands. She performed Light of Dreams, the theme song from Shenbing Kids, a Chinese animated series that premiered in 2007. The performance gave spectators an unexpected musical celebration.

The moment showed a lighter side of a fierce competitor. Fans who had cheered throughout the final now got a song. Big tennis finals rarely end with an impromptu musical performance during the trophy ceremony, making this celebration particularly memorable.

Zheng also appeared relieved and delighted after winning her first WTA 1000 title. The victory followed a difficult period marked by injuries and interrupted competition. Her emotional celebration offered fans another reason to appreciate the achievement.

Andreeva is only 19 yet already owns a French Open title. She became the youngest Roland Garros women's champion since Monica Seles in 1992. Players with that record often speak with calm confidence and humor.

Her joke also showed a sense of perspective. She did not blame fans or complain about the noise. She noted what she heard and moved on with grace, a balance that is rare for teens.

Humor can protect a competitor after a loss. It turns disappointment into a story people can smile about. Andreeva chose that path instead of hiding her feelings, which made her far more relatable to fans.

Tennis crowds sit very close to the action. Their noise can lift one player and rattle another. That energy changes how every point feels on court, giving home stars extra fuel and visitors extra weight.

Partisan crowds are normal in sport. Fans cheer for their own heroes, and nobody should be shocked. Still, a few friendly cheers for the visitor can warm the room and show respect for the game.

That is the heart of her joke. She never demanded a crowd on her side and simply hoped for one small shout of support in a packed arena. That modest wish made the line charming.

Zheng's China Open victory marked an important comeback after a difficult year affected by injuries. However, she withdrew from the Wuhan Open on October 12, citing a right shoulder injury and fatigue. Her immediate priority is recovering while building on her historic Beijing title.

Andreeva also withdrew from Wuhan following the final, citing a scheduling change. The 19-year-old reached a career-high No. 3 in the WTA rankings after her Beijing performance and remains one of the leading young players on the women's tour.

A future rematch between the two would bring plenty of interest. Zheng has now won both of their meetings, including the 2026 China Open final. Andreeva will have another opportunity to challenge her if they meet again, perhaps before a more evenly divided crowd.

Little-known fact: Andreeva told reporters before the 2026 Madrid Open that she had finished three kits and was on her fourth. She can spend about three hours placing the tiny pieces one by one, and she avoids huge sets because she has no space for them.

Andreeva joked that she hoped to hear one "let's go Mirra" during the final.

Zheng became the first Chinese woman to win the China Open title.

The home crowd roared for Zheng from start to finish.

Andreeva stayed polite and thanked fans for their support.

Zheng celebrated by singing karaoke for the Beijing crowd.
